544225|2026-06.headline: Ola Electric Q1 FY27 deliveries nearly doubled QoQ to ~39,200 units, Auto revenue ₹455 crore (+72% QoQ), Auto gross margin 30.5%.
544225|2026-06.overview: Ola returned to volume growth in Q1 FY27, with deliveries of ~39,200 units (nearly 2x QoQ) and orders of ~44,000, while electric two-wheeler registrations grew 97% against a market up ~17% QoQ, lifting share from 5.1% to 8.4%. Auto revenue rose 72% QoQ to ₹455 crore with gross profit of ₹139 crore and Auto gross margin held at 30.5%. Consolidated opex fell 22% QoQ to ₹333 crore (including a ~₹55 crore one-time reversal of a Cell ACC PLI penalty provision), and adjusted operating EBITDA improved to –₹195 crore from –₹326 crore in Q4 FY26. Management pivoted Auto distribution from company-owned to a multi-channel model with dealers, with the first batch slated to go live on Janmashtami (4 September), and reiterated a Cell gigafactory ramp to 6 GWh.

financial_highlights.change: -22% QoQ from ₹428 crore in Q4; ~₹380 crore excluding ~₹55 crore one-time PLI provision reversal
from 5.1%; Ola registrations +97% QoQ vs market ~+17%

segments.name: Auto (scooters, motorcycles)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹455 crore (+72% QoQ), gross profit ₹139 crore, gross margin 30.5%. Premium business recovering; motorcycles starting to grow in northern plains. Roadster a small minority of sales; 9.1 kWh variant supply constrained by 4680 cell shortage.

segments.name: Cell business
segments.commentary: 4680 NMC cells commercially deployed; a few hundred thousand cells produced and in customer vehicles. Production paused in Q1 to take capacity from 2.5 GWh to 6 GWh; restart expected later in August. 46100 LFP cell BIS-certified. Yields high-70s to ~80% at pause, target >90% within a quarter of restart.

segments.name: Ola Shakti / Mahashakti (energy storage)
segments.commentary: Only a few hundred NMC-based Shakti units delivered in Q1, no meaningful revenue; NMC version pared back on sub-target margins. Shakti Gen 2 (LFP) to be announced 15 August. First Mahashakti MoU with Axis Energy for 20 GWh over 5-6 years; early Mahashakti revenue hoped for Q3 or Q4.

Auto gross margin target ~30-32%; expected to hold above 30% over next one to two quarters and improve as commodity prices ease.
Opex to fall to ₹300-325 crore range over the next couple of quarters.
Gross margin steady to slightly growing and volumes steady to slightly growing while cutting opex; no formal FY volume guidance.

Service revenue target ~₹400-500 crore by FY2027-28 from installed base of over one million customers.
Capex beyond Cell project about ₹30-50 crore; ₹50 crore used as target number.
Pending 4680-cell Roadster deliveries to be completed over Q2 and Q3 FY27.

Dealer model: ~500 current touchpoints (analyst figure); company stores to become fewer, larger experience centres; ~1,000 expressions of interest from prospective dealers; 20-30 dealers engaged for about a month before announcement.
Service challenges attributed to parts availability (vendor issues, geopolitical factors); dealers to stock parts on cash-and-carry basis.
Shakti to be sold through company stores, automotive dealers and industry-specific inverter/battery channels.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ASP decline sharply sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed about 90% to product mix; ASP guided at ~₹1.25 lakh ±5%.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year volume guidance and Q4 exit rate?
qa_highlights.answer: No formal guidance; management expects steady growth but declined quarter-on-quarter numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Own-cell penetration and Shakti revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: A few thousand own-cell vehicles on road; about 3 of ~9-10 SKUs use 4680 cells. Shakti Gen 1 (NMC) had no meaningful revenue; Gen 2 (LFP) on 15 August.

qa_highlights.question: Capex for the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Beyond the Cell project, capex ~₹30-50 crore, with ₹50 crore as target; Auto needs hardly any capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why did depreciation fall QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Policy aligned to industry norms after aggressive depreciation; delta ~₹10-20 crore, no write-off mentioned.

qa_highlights.question: LFP vs NMC mix and 20 GWh expansion timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Almost all Auto to move to LFP over time, ~20% of Auto stays NMC; Shakti/Mahashakti all LFP. 20 GWh expansion (prismatic) in FY27 with separate Cell-company equity; yields high-70s to ~80% at pause.

qa_highlights.question: Scale of energy storage opportunity and Axis Energy MoU?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites CEA estimate of ~400 GWh needed over 5-6 years, which it views as an underestimate; Mahashakti expected to have round-trip efficiency a few points above peers and safety above standard 5 MWh containers.

qa_highlights.question: Roadster contribution?

544225|2026-09.headline: Ola Electric Q2 FY27 revenue fell to Rs 421 crore with gross margin steady near 30%, as management says demand now exceeds supply.
544225|2026-09.overview: Revenue from operations was Rs 421 crore versus Rs 455 crore in Q1, with gross margin of Rs 126 crore (about 30%) versus Rs 139 crore (30.5%). Operating expenses were Rs 369 crore, or about Rs 390 crore after adding back a one-time Rs 57 crore credit in Q1. Operating cash flow improved to negative Rs 188 crore from negative Rs 215 crore, and consolidated debt fell from Rs 3,132 crore (Dec 2024) to Rs 1,800 crore (Sep 2026). Management said the company moved its D2C stores to a dealership model, with 255 dealer partners and 319 stores as of 8 November, and that the constraint is now supply rather than demand.

vs negative Rs 195 crore in Q1
vs loss of Rs 336 crore in Q1

segments.name: Auto (EV scooters, D2C to dealer)
segments.commentary: Dealer count reached 255 partners and 319 stores by 8 November, with a target of 450 stores by December and about 700+ by March 2027. Channel inventory is about 15 days, and management says the company is moving to a dealer model with negative working capital.

segments.name: Cell (gigafactory)
segments.commentary: Commissioned 6 GWh capacity (3.5 GW added) with COD on 23 September. NMC yields are in the mid-70s% with a target of mid-80s over the next couple of months; the target is 90%. PLI benefits are expected from next quarter, and the ACC PLI has been extended to 2031.

guidance_outlook: Gross margin expected to fall to about 4% as dealer commissions are deducted, while operating margin is expected to improve to about 3% and beyond.
Company stores to close by December, with opex falling further as the store network shuts; management expects the auto business to reach near- to mid-term free cash flow.
Cell business: NMC integration into own auto products from next quarter, with own LFP cell production towards the end of FY27 or early Q1; 30% of auto volumes to use NMC and 70% LFP.
FY28 planning assumption of about 5 kWh average pack per vehicle, so 2-3 GWh of cell output implies roughly 400-500k vehicles.

Gen 3/4 product with 4680 cells is targeted for Q4, with launch timing dependent on demand and supply.

Cell utilisation to ramp step by step as NMC and LFP cells are integrated into own products first, then into energy storage.
Capex to scale from 6 GWh to 20 GWh is expected to be much smaller than the 0-6 GWh build; the factory is designed for 20 GWh.
Delivery of the 4680-based vehicle is targeted for Q4 FY27, with the launch date subject to testing and demand.
Rs 5,000 crore IPO plus Rs 2,500 crore pre-IPO equity, plus QIP and rights issue; rights issue 60% paid, with 40% call date not yet announced.
demand_pricing: Management says demand exceeds supply: about 5,000 paid-order vehicles had deliveries pushed by a week into October due to charger unavailability.
Management said about 45,000 vehicles were ready but could not be booked as revenue in Q2 because chargers were not available.
Gross margin decline was mainly from commodity costs, partly offset by a price increase.
Dealer-channel early markets show market share above pre-transition levels, per management; dealer re-ordering is ramping.
Management says its bill of materials is 15-20% below competitors (around Rs 80-85k per vehicle), attributed to in-house engineering and vertical integration.

qa_highlights.question: What were the Q2 vehicle volumes, and is the QoQ gross margin dip due to commodities or mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Volumes were about 35,000-36,000 booked; about 45,000 paid vehicles slipped to October. The margin dip was mainly commodity-driven, with a partial price increase offsetting part of it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the battery pack size used to derive FY28 unit volumes from 2-3 GWh of cell output?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said to plan on about 5 kWh per vehicle for FY28, versus about 3.8 kWh today, implying roughly 400-500k vehicles from 2-3 GWh.

qa_highlights.question: What is the dealer commission and its effect on the auto margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the introductory dealer commission will fall over the next two to three quarters, and gross margin will decline but operating margin will rise. It declined to confirm the Rs 11,000 per-vehicle estimate.

qa_highlights.question: What gives confidence in the ramp from mid-70s% yields to 90%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yields are already in the mid-70s% for NMC with a clear roadmap to mid-80s over the next couple of months and 90% later. It said the cell business has been in development since 2020.

qa_highlights.question: How will GST refunds affect cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 30-40% of the receivable is inverted duty structure and the rest will be consumed in future business. Approval timelines are expected to fall from 3-4 months to 1-2 months from 1 November.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 4680 product be delivered on time, and what is the cost advantage of in-house cells?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the product is targeted for Q4 and launch timing depends on demand. The in-house cell is expected to deliver about a 20% cost advantage over 2170 cells at scale.

risks_watch: Supply and component constraints (chargers, supplier ramp-up) are holding back deliveries; the paid order backlog must be cleared.
Dealer margin structure is introductory and could change; gross margin is guided lower.
NMC yield ramp from mid-70s% toward 90%, plus PLI receipt timing and the cell business's dependence on external equity for the 20 GWh expansion.
Working capital and GST refund timing; about 30-40% of the receivable is tied to inverted duty and may not convert to cash quickly.

544226|2026-03.headline: FirstCry Q4 FY26: consol revenue up 12% to ₹8,547 Cr for FY26; Q4 adjusted EBITDA up 18% to ₹118.7 Cr amid India gross margin pressure.
544226|2026-03.overview: Brainbees (FirstCry) reported Q4 and FY26 with consolidated FY26 revenue up 12% to ₹8,547 Cr, adjusted EBITDA up 24% to about ₹486 Cr, and free cash flow positive for the full year. India multi-channel grew 11.4% in Q4 but gross margin fell on diaper price competition from quick-commerce and horizontal players, plus a transitory manufacturing hit from rupee depreciation and crude-linked inputs. Management says the offline channel grew about 15% in Q4 after a product-mix shift, and that RocketBees and Qwik delivery initiatives are lifting service levels, with the benefit expected to show in FY27. International losses fell 35% in FY26 and GlobalBees core categories grew 28%.

segments.name: India multi-channel
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue +11.4% and FY26 revenue +9%; GMV +11% in FY26, crossing $1 billion for the first time. Management says the segment stayed PAT and cash flow positive in FY26. Non-diapering is over 85% of GMV; diapering (about 15% of business) faces heavy price competition.

segments.name: International (UAE and KSA)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue above $100 million, growing about 10% in FY26; Q4 revenue +9%. Gross margin rose 240 bps for FY26 (470 bps in Q4). Management did not give a timeline for reaching break-even.

segments.name: GlobalBees
segments.commentary: FY26 consolidated revenue +20% (organic, after brand rationalisation) and core categories +28%. Adjusted EBITDA post-corporate expenses was 5.8% of revenue in Q4 (₹26.5 Cr) and about 3% for FY26 after ESOP cost. Brand rationalisation is expected to finish by end Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Others (preschool)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue +11% with EBITDA margin about 27% (vs 24% in FY25). Preschools more than doubled from 208 at end FY24, and enrolled students are almost 3x in two years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 India multi-channel GMV and revenue growth guided to be much superior to FY26; management expects sequential quarterly improvement to continue.
India multi-channel FY27 EBITDA (rupee terms) guided to grow double digits, per management's 'should' answer; margin expansion expected outside diapering.
Gross margin loss from the Q3 diaper competition (about 140 bps) expected to take 4-6 quarters to reverse; manufacturing-related loss expected to be recovered from Q2 FY27 via pass-through.
Company-owned and FOFO stores: about 100 openings planned in FY27 after pausing COCO openings in FY26 (10 COCO stores added in FY26).
Qwik expected to reach roughly 10% of total B2C online shipments over FY27; RocketBees already at 40%+ of online delivery volume, with a target of 45-50% by mid-2026.
Continued international loss reduction in FY27; management aims to take losses to zero as early as possible.
capex_capacity: RocketBees own-network coverage grew from 13 cities (Q2) to 22 (Q3) to 62 cities (Q4); management aims to cross 50 cities by next quarter-end.
Qwik quick-delivery pilot began 1 Dec 2025 and now runs in 5 cities; it delivers in under 3 hours and is already over 20% of online orders in the covered catchments.
Logistics cost front-loading of about 40-60 bps for a few quarters until RocketBees and Qwik networks mature.
Asset-light delivery model: dedicated regional first-mile and mid-mile partners and dedicated last-mile partners on in-house technology.
Offline initiative (width-to-depth product assortment change) went live in Q4 FY26 and drove about 15% offline GMV growth.
Management says on-time delivery exceeds 92%.
demand_pricing: Diapering faces irrational price competition from quick-commerce and horizontal platforms (listed and unlisted); management expects this to last 4-6 quarters.
Q4 online GMV grew about 10.5%, and online growth held at about 11-12% across all four quarters of FY26. Offline GMV grew about 15% in Q4.
Annual unique transacting customers in India multi-channel: 11 million.
India multi-channel Q4 orders +10% and GMV +12%; AOV in International is about 4x India's.
Management says the Middle East has seen some moderation in consumer sentiment and import complexities, but it is 'beyond anyone's control'.
Ages 6-12 is the fastest-growing age cohort in India multi-channel.

qa_highlights.question: What share of orders now goes through FirstCry's own delivery network, and what is the logistics cost increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Share rose from about 28% at end Q3 to over 40% at end March 2026, with a target of 45-50% by mid-year. Logistics cost is front-loaded by about 40-60 bps for a few quarters until networks mature.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the company pause COCO store openings in FY26, and what is the FY27 plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Openings were paused for capital efficiency given macro conditions. Management plans about 100 stores in FY27 across COCO and FOFO formats, citing the best offline growth in seven quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How is the gross margin pressure in diapering split between competition and input inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: The 140 bps Q3 competitive hit has continued into Q4. The remaining manufacturing-related hit from rupee depreciation and crude-linked inputs is transitory and expected to be recovered from Q2 FY27 as prices are passed through.

qa_highlights.question: Is the online growth slowdown structural, given offline grew faster than the 11% overall?
qa_highlights.answer: Online GMV grew about 10.5% in Q4 and 11-12% through FY26. Management expects RocketBees and Qwik to lift online growth in FY27, with results lagging. Product mix between online and offline has not changed.

qa_highlights.question: Can India multi-channel EBITDA grow double digits in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, citing recovery of the manufacturing hit by Q2 (three quarters of benefit), continued margin expansion in the non-diaper categories, and operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Middle East situation affecting international revenue and break-even?
qa_highlights.answer: Consumer sentiment has moderated and import complexities have emerged. Management sees this as an opportunity to optimise discounting and marketing and to improve home-brand mix, and says the focus remains sustainable growth over top-line chasing.

risks_watch: Diaper price war from quick-commerce and horizontal platforms could keep gross margins under pressure beyond the 4-6 quarter window management has given.
Management has tied the FY27 recovery to a Q2 pass-through of manufacturing costs, with rupee depreciation and crude prices as the swing factors.
Middle East consumer sentiment and import complexities could slow International, where revenue growth was about 9-10%.
Online growth has run at about 10-12% and needs to accelerate in FY27 for the stated guidance to hold.
GlobalBees brand rationalisation is due to finish by end Q1 FY27; the consolidated growth figure will lag until then.
Management declined to quantify AI-driven savings, saying the number will come in later quarterly updates. It also said there have been no buyback or acquisition discussions.

544226|2026-06.headline: Brainbees Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 13% to ₹2,106 crore, but India multi-channel gross margin fell ~260 bps YoY, holding adjusted EBITDA margin at 4.24%.
544226|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY to ₹2,106 crore, with GMV up 12% to ₹2,807 crore and AUTC up 10% to 11.8 million. Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 4.24% from 4.98%, and gross margin dropped to 36.5% from 38.5%, mainly from India multi-channel diapering competition and manufacturing cost pass-through lag. Management said diapering competition is easing and that the crude/rupee cost pass-through completes by end-Q2, but gave no firm timeline for margin recovery. Growth drivers cited were RocketBees (over 50% of online shipments), FC Qwik (125,000 shipments in June across 12 cities) and offline GMV growth of 15%.

segments.name: International (Middle East)
segments.commentary: Revenue +12% YoY, AUTC +7%, GMV +9%. Adjusted EBITDA loss reduced 22% YoY; loss-to-revenue improved from 10% to 7%. Management targets EBITDA neutrality but gave no timeline.

segments.name: GlobalBees
segments.commentary: Revenue roughly flat due to a planned warehouse and inventory transition for one core brand, expected to complete in Q2 with growth recovering from Q3. Adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 3.9% from 1%.

segments.commentary: Revenue +47% to ₹19 crore and adjusted EBITDA +65% to ₹5 crore. Over 500 preschools; management targets at least 1,000 over the next couple of years, organically, with no M&A being evaluated.

544227|2026-03.headline: Unicommerce FY26 revenue rose 51.6% to INR204.3 crore, but Q4 adjusted EBITDA growth slowed to 7.8% as investments step up.
544227|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew 51.6% to INR204.3 crore and adjusted EBITDA rose 54.5% to INR43.9 crore, with FY26 being the first full year consolidating Shipway. Q4 revenue grew 14% YoY to INR51.6 crore, but adjusted EBITDA grew only 7.8% to INR9.6 crore and PAT grew 1.6% to INR3.4 crore after management began stepping up growth investments in Q4. Management guided to lower adjusted EBITDA and PAT over the next two quarters, while expecting higher full-year operational profitability in FY27 than FY26. Management also disclosed it is evaluating a merger with Shipway Technology Private Limited.

qa_highlights.question: Current capacity utilisation and margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 sales were 162,000 tonnes against 200,000 tonnes capacity (about 80%, about 88% of utilisable capacity). Capacity is now about 221,000 tonnes and Q1 volume was 38,499 tonnes (about 80% of 50,000 tonnes quarterly capacity). Margin gains are expected mainly in FY28, not immediately, as new plants carry upfront costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise QIP when cash generation appears sufficient, and what capex is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited working capital needs for larger orders and a desire to raise funds once for the next two years. Capex is about INR129 crores in FY27 and INR133 crores in FY28. Timing is undecided and could fall within about 4 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why are some energy-sector orders on 15-16 month execution periods, and what is the export contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: The orders are for HVDC valve halls from EPC contractors on variable-price terms, and site clearances take about 6 months versus 2-3 months normally. Q1 exports were about INR10-12 crores of INR460 crores, and management targets about 10% of turnover from exports in 1-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was finance cost up sharply, and what is the debt position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company has no debt. Finance cost rose because interest income fell as IPO cash was spent on capex, and a one-time bank processing fee was paid on enhanced non-fund-based limits. Non-fund limit utilisation was 82% versus 64% a year earlier.

risks_watch: Quarterly revenue lumpiness: management guides to about INR600 crores per quarter for the next 3-4 quarters, needing about INR1,700 crores in 9 months; Q1 was INR460 crores, so the H1 ramp is a key test.
Margin pressure from steel prices and shortages (linked to the Iran war), freight, labour and erection prices; management expects margin gains mainly in FY28 and EBITDA margin was 8.6%.

Execution risk on new capacity: Gujarat Phase 2 by October 2026, heavy structure commercial production around end-August/early-September 2026, and utilisation of heavy structures unclear until about March 2027.
Heavy structure order pipeline is still early; management is taking a cautious 5-6 month approach and the INR200 crore FY28 uplift depends on it.
Other income falling as IPO cash is spent on capex; PAT flat at INR28 crores, and finance cost up; watch how QIP proceeds (INR250 crores, timing undecided) affect treasury income and capex.
Competitive intensity and price pressure; management says competition is intensifying but the pie is growing, and it is prioritising profitability over revenue growth.
Revenue guidance kept at INR2,150-2,200 crores despite a 20.7% Q1 rise; management may revisit in 3-4 months, so watch for a guidance upgrade or a revision at the next call.
key_quotes: So we are well on track for our projections.
So that is our decision.
We want to revise our projections for '27 -'28 to INR2,700 crores from INR2,500 crores.

But I'm not very sure that it will show immediate results this year because we have to also, whenever we open new plants and new areas like we have done, Gujarat and heavy structure, a lot of expense goes into that in advance of actually the sale happening.
544232|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident on demand, order book and the expansion plan, but cautious on near-term revenue and guidance, repeatedly saying it would not revise FY27 guidance until more data arrives. It was evasive on the specific quarterly revenue shortfall and on margin timing, attributing both to seasonality and new-plant costs.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Capacity is about 221,000 t/yr after Kheda Phase 1, heavy structures trial runs are underway, and FY26 utilisation was about 80% of installed capacity, so new lines are already firmly scheduled.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides FY27 volume up about 18% to roughly 190,000 t from 162,000 t in FY26, backed by a INR1,864 crore order book and new capacity coming online.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: The QIP was raised to INR250 crores from INR100 crores, with use of funds already allocated to heavy structures, Gujarat Plant 2 and the Canada JV, and FY27/FY28 capex at INR129 crores and INR133 crores; utilisation of about 80% also supports more capacity.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management says it may beat FY27 guidance of INR2,150-2,200 crores and will revisit in 3-4 months, while FY28 was already raised to INR2,700 crores from INR2,500 crores; Q1 revenue of INR460 crores (+20.7%) needs about INR1,700 crores more in 9 months to hit the run-rate.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.when: Production by July-end 2027; exports ~10% of turnover in 1-2
rows.why: The 15,000 t JV plant could yield about $20-23 million at full capacity, and management targets exports at about 10% of turnover in 1-2 years, though Phase 1 is not until mid-2027.

rows.label: Heavy structures order pipeline and FY28 uplift
rows.why: Management expects INR100-150 crores of FY27 heavy structures revenue and about INR200 crores in FY28, but says the pipeline is early and it is taking a cautious 5-6 month approach.

rows.label: No debt; treasury income falling as IPO cash is spent
rows.why: Interest income fell as about INR240 crores of capex was spent against INR180 crores raised in the IPO, so other income has dropped and PAT was flat at INR28 crores, while the company remains debt-free.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the INR1,864 crore order book and the expansion plan, but cautious on guidance and would not revise FY27 until more data arrives; analysts pressed on the Q1 shortfall versus the INR600 crore quarterly run-rate, margin timing and the QIP rationale.

544232|2026-09.headline: Interarch FY26 revenue rose 31% to Rs 1,898 crore with EBITDA margin steady at 9.3%; FY27 guided to Rs 2,150-2,200 crore.
544232|2026-09.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was about Rs 500 crore, up 8.7% QoQ, as capacity was already fully utilised from Q3 and Q4 did not rise seasonally. Q4 EBITDA was Rs 53 crore (10.5% margin) versus Rs 49 crore in Q3, with management citing Rs 5-5.5 crore of one-time costs (labour code provision, certifications, professional fees for heavy structure bids). Full-year PAT was Rs 135 crore versus Rs 108 crore, with a higher effective tax rate due to a gratuity tax deduction not recurring and a change in Section 145A treatment. Order book stood at over Rs 1,700 crore as of 30 April 2026, to be executed in about nine months, and management said capacity, not demand, is the constraint.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 49 crore in prior quarter; margin 10.5%

financial_highlights.value: over Rs 1,700 crore as of 30 April 2026
financial_highlights.change: about Rs 40-50 crore higher than last disclosed; about Rs 1,650 crore QoQ per management

segments.name: Pre-engineered buildings (PEB)
segments.commentary: Virtually the entire Rs 1,700 crore order book is PEB; realisation about Rs 120 per kg, expected to hold on an annual basis. Industrial buildings were about 87% of FY26 sales per the investor presentation, as cited in Q&A.

segments.name: Heavy structures (HSS)
segments.commentary: Plant in Andhra Pradesh to start trial production in June and commercial production in July 2026, capacity 18,000-20,000 tonnes; realisation about Rs 95-100 per kg. First order of Rs 102 crore (Rajpath government buildings, supply from September) announced after the quarter.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Revenue was about 3-3.5% of total; Rs 30-35 crore of export orders in hand, with a target of Rs 50-60 crore of new orders in FY27. North America margins are better and payments are advance or LC-based; no North American revenue in Q4.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of Rs 2,150-2,200 crore (about 15% growth, upper end of earlier range); FY28 target Rs 2,500 crore, which management said may be revised after heavy structure capacity is operating.
FY27 net PAT margin guided at 7-7.5%, with management saying current margins should be maintained.
EBITDA margin expected around 9.3-9.4% on an annual basis; management aspires to 9.5-10% over time.
Gujarat PEB plant (fifth integrated plant, about Rs 2,500 crore capacity) to start commercial production in July 2026; Phase 2 by end of 2026.
Heavy structure plant: 10,000-12,000 tonnes possible in FY27 (about Rs 120-130 crore), full-year potential Rs 200-210 crore.
Capacity to rise from about 180,000 tonnes per year to about 40,000 tonnes per quarter additions in stages, reaching 60,000 tonnes by Nov-Dec 2026 per management.
Proposed 50:50 JV with Canadian partner for a 100% export unit (open web joist), expected to start in about 12 months.
QIP under consideration; fundraise expected in the next two to three months, primarily for heavy structure Phases 2 and 3.
capex_capacity: Gujarat PEB plant: building complete for both phases; machinery delivery from May, installation by early June, trial production June, commercial production July 2026; Phase 2 machinery by end-2026. Delay of about 1.5 months due to high water table and foundation redesign.
Andhra Pradesh heavy structure plant: Phase 1 production July-August 2026; Phases 2 and 3 being accelerated, targeted by end of FY27 or early FY28; land bought in Gujarat for a further plant.
Current capacity about 160,000 tonnes/year from four full plants, about 180,000 tonnes including outsourcing; Q4 utilisation essentially full.
Heavy structure machinery imported from Germany and Italy; robotics and automation for welding under evaluation.
demand_pricing: Management said there is no slowdown from customers; pipeline 1 (orders expected within 60 days) about Rs 800-900 crore, pipeline 2 (bid, decision in 2-7 months) about Rs 3,500 crore.
Order intake is capacity-constrained; management said it will only take orders it can deliver within the 9-month order book horizon.

Steel prices rose sharply in Jan-Mar 2026; management said pricing is job-specific, with steel bought in advance, and that prices should soften from May-June, with the net effect averaging out over four quarters.

Management attributes sales shortfall vs expectation to Q3 having been unusually strong and Q4 capacity-capped; about Rs 20-25 crore revenue held back in Q4 due to site clearances after labour left during the March LPG shortage and elections in Bengal.
Customers are shifting toward value and delivery over price; management expects margin improvement from larger, value-focused clients, though some large projects are split among 2-3 players.

qa_highlights.question: What is steel supplier concentration and were there disruptions from steel mill shutdowns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no disruption to projects; relationships with SAIL, JSW and AMNS (25-26 years) and informal long-term price arrangements helped. Minor delays were from labour shortage in March.

qa_highlights.question: Why were cash flows from operations negative in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Larger milestone-driven orders (five to seven orders above Rs 100 crore) raised receivables, and inventory was built ahead of expected steel price rises; management expects OCF to turn positive quickly, with tighter payment terms.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Q4 EBITDA margin fall short of 12-15% expectations, and what drove the one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Q3 base was unusually high; one-offs of Rs 5-6 crore (labour code provision Rs 3.5 crore, certifications Rs 2-2.5 crore, high-rise bid costs) would have lifted margin to about 9.7%.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the tax rate higher and will it persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Effective rate about 27% vs 24% last year, from a non-recurring gratuity deduction and a Section 145A inventory change; management said there will be no further hit going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Can export margins be higher than domestic?
qa_highlights.answer: Nearby markets (Africa, Myanmar) priced near Indian levels with LC or advance payments; North America offers higher margins with no erection risk, but no US or Canadian revenue was booked in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why is order inflow not growing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the order book already covers about nine months of capacity; it will take more orders only as new capacity comes online, and market demand is not the constraint.

risks_watch: Working capital: negative FY26 OCF tied to receivables on large milestone-based orders and inventory build; watch for OCF turning positive.
Gujarat and Andhra commissioning timelines (July 2026 start), given a prior one-month slip and phase-2 machinery dependence on hiring.
Labour availability; management flagged manpower shortage and migrant labour disruption as the key FY27 challenge.
Heavy structure economics unproven: HSS EBITDA per kg not yet established and FY27 revenue guidance excludes it, with a revision expected by end-2026.
Steel price volatility; management says it is managed through job-specific pricing but Q1 margin could move 0.1-0.2 points.
QIP timing and size; proceeds mainly for heavy structure expansion.
544232|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and detailed on capacity and order visibility, with a defensive tone on the Q4 sales shortfall and negative operating cash flow, which management attributed to timing and large-order mix. Management was evasive on FY28 guidance and on HSS economics, saying it would revisit them once heavy structure output is being sold.

I think we are saying that Quarter 3 to Quarter 4, the growth has been 8.7% and maybe that has led to a little disappointment.
So, the 3rd Quarter was better, not because the 4th Quarter was bad.
So, we are basically saying that whatever margins we are making currently, that margin we should maintain.

rows.why: Order book above Rs 1,700 crore as of 30 April 2026 to be executed in about nine months, with pipeline 1 of Rs 800-900 crore expected within 60 days.

rows.why: Export revenue is only about 3-3.5% of total and Rs 30-35 crore of export orders are in hand against a Rs 50-60 crore new-order target, with North America margins better.

tone.note: Management was confident on capacity coming live, order visibility and the Rs 2,150-2,200 crore FY27 guide, but defensive on the Q4 sales shortfall and negative OCF and evasive on FY28 and HSS economics; analysts pressed on margins, tax, working capital and why order inflow is not growing.

544235|2026-06.headline: Orient Technologies Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA rose 161% QoQ to Rs 15.42 crores, margin 7.57%, with profit of Rs 5.17 crores versus a Q4 FY26 loss.
544235|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was Rs 201.92 crores, up 9.70% QoQ from Rs 184.07 crores in Q4 FY26. EBITDA margin expanded 438 bps to 7.57%, and the company returned to profit of Rs 5.17 crores against a Rs 4.99 crore loss in Q4. Management said supply conditions were stable and pricing competitive, and that FY27 would be a year of steady sequential improvement rather than a sharp turnaround. The order book was about Rs 375.43 crores, with most billing expected in Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not give forward guidance; cited operational efficiency and margin-led deal selection, and said current margin levels should be sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: Execution timing of the Rs 375 crore order book?

qa_highlights.question: Minimum sustainable gross margin?

544235|2026-09.headline: Orient Technologies Q2 FY27 revenue rose 8.84% QoQ to Rs 219.77 crore while EBITDA margin expanded to 7.57%, driven by services mix.
544235|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached Rs 219.77 crore in Q2 FY27, up 8.84% QoQ, with services revenue up 24.95% QoQ to Rs 130.99 crore while product revenue fell to Rs 88.78 crore from Rs 97.09 crore. EBITDA rose 45.6% QoQ to Rs 22.45 crore, though the margin is stated as 7.57% against the 10.20% figure quoted for Q1 (the call also describes margin as "about 10%" and as having expanded 263 bps, which are internally inconsistent with the stated figures). PAT rose to Rs 11.72 crore from Rs 5.17 crore. Management attributed the shift to managed services amid infrastructure product delivery delays and cost increases; H1 revenue was down about 14% YoY, which management attributed to infrastructure weakness.

Rs 132 crore products, Rs 199 crore services; expected to be built by Mar 31, 2027

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the strong services contribution and how will it build?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said infrastructure product challenges led to a strategy shift toward managed services (data centre, cloud, cyber, infra management, digital transformation). Services revenue rose from Rs 88.78 crore to Rs 130.99 crore QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: How should margins look over the next 2 to 3 years as managed services grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give forward numbers, saying only that the managed services strategy will remain constant.

qa_highlights.question: What working capital steps are planned and how will they support cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is debt-free and targets remaining debt-free by March 2027; working capital focus is DaaS, where customers are being chosen selectively and screened by a credit agency.

qa_highlights.question: Why did H1 FY27 revenue fall about 14% YoY, and will FY27 exceed FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the dip to infrastructure business challenges and reduced aggressive pursuit of deals; said it would not comment on FY27 vs FY26 but expects QoQ growth to continue.

qa_highlights.question: Services versus products split of the Rs 331 crore order book and average services tenure?

544238|2026-03.headline: Premier Energies FY26 revenue rose 20.7% to INR8,026 crore and PAT 61.1% to INR1,510 crore, with order book at INR14,010 crore (+66% YoY).

segments.commentary: Module capacity 11.1 GW; management says utilisation is about 75% (roughly 7-7.5 GW). The 5.6 GW Sitarampur plant uses about 40% less manpower per MW than existing plants. Management expects DCR share to rise every quarter.

segments.commentary: Acquired 51% stake; FY revenue INR423 crore and PAT INR45 crore. Plant due for completion in July 2026; management says it has secured some first orders, and ramp-up is expected to take about two years.

segments.commentary: Inverter business pursued via a JV with SMA SGS (first preference) after K-Solar deal lapsed. BESS capacity pace is deliberately slowed due to imports at about 11% duty; localisation policy expected around FY28.

FY27 capex of INR5,100 crore across cells, ingot wafers, batteries and inverters; a roughly INR12,000 crore capex plan is spread over three years from FY26.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the DCR portal is a verification and traceability tool, not a sales indicator, and that the cell vs DCR module mix changes quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cost trends and the bill of materials change for modules?
qa_highlights.answer: Cell costs rose to about 6-6.2 cents from 3.5 cents, passed through on non-DCR modules. DCR margins are maintained through scale and mix. Glass cost unchanged; aluminium (about 11% of module cost) rose slightly, offset by design changes.

qa_highlights.question: How will the 7 GW line and order book convert?

qa_highlights.answer: Management said no material risk, because C&I orders in the book deliver after October-November and any delay of a quarter would not affect them.

544238|2026-06.headline: Premier Energies Q1 FY27 revenue rose 34% YoY to INR2,508 crores, PAT up 53% to INR472 crores at an 18.8% margin.

The 5.6 GW Seetharampur module plant is operational, while the 7 GW TOPCon cell line is in late commissioning with trial runs expected later in August. Order wins were INR3,011 crores in the quarter, taking the total order book to INR15,000 crores including transformers. Management said the ALMM extension to December triggered a surge in non-DCR module orders, while DCR is sold out through FY28 per management.

segments.commentary: Q1 revenue INR110 crores, PAT INR18 crores; management expects business to roughly treble over three years, with transformer capacity going from 4 GVA to 16.25 GVA by FY28. Last year's revenue was about INR400 crores.

qa_highlights.answer: Blended overloading of 1.2-1.25x (KUSUM B at 1.0x, KUSUM C at 1.3-1.5x). Management expects about 1.2-1.3 GW per quarter of rooftop and 6-8 GW AC (possibly more than 8 GW) of KUSUM over nine months; total about 23-24 GW DC over nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Why sell cells rather than convert them into DCR modules and capture the margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said legacy cell contracts signed earlier must be honoured; as the 7 GW cell line starts, DCR module output will rise and cell sales will fall. Q1 module orders were mostly for modules.

qa_highlights.question: Will C&I demand be deferred by the ALMM extension, and is DCR capacity blocked?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said C&I clients are already blocking capacity for FY28 and are not deferring; DCR is sold out with FY28 sales underway.

qa_highlights.question: Is the transformer margin normal level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the normalised transformer margin is about 15%; the prior quarter's 22% was boosted by steel and copper price increases and hedged inventory.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any block sale or QIP risk?

Naidupeta ALMM enrolment inspection (expected third week of November) and the 70% CUF target by March 2027.

544239|2026-03.headline: ECOS Q4 FY26 revenue up 16.65% to INR2,067.6 million, EBITDA down to INR241.5 million; FY27 guided to 18-20% growth at 11-13% margin.
544239|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 16.65% YoY to INR2,067.60 million, while EBITDA declined to INR241.53 million from INR264.67 million in Q4 FY25, reflecting continued investment in people, technology and leadership. For FY26, revenue rose 23.58% to INR8,081.58 million and EBITDA was INR939.29 million, with margins hit by higher manpower cost, tech spend, ETS price competition and a one-time doubtful-debt provision of about INR80 million. Management said the Middle East crisis dented CCR growth in March, and guided FY27 revenue growth of 18-20% and EBITDA margin of 11-13%, with cost growth expected to be lower than revenue growth. Analysts pressed on margin compression, falling revenue per trip and competitive pricing in ETS; management attributed the trend partly to shorter trips and airport transfers.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR264.67 million in Q4 FY25 (decline)
vs 4.04 million in FY25, approx. +29% YoY

segments.name: ETS (employee transportation services)
segments.commentary: 58% of FY26 revenue and 57% in Q4 FY26. Stable demand from IT/ITES and a strong surge from GCC clients, but competitive pricing pressure was most visible here.

segments.name: CCR (chauffeur-driven car rental)
segments.commentary: 42% of FY26 revenue and 43% in Q4 FY26. Growth slowed in March after the Middle East crisis, though management says it bounced back; management described CCR as a brand-led business with a premium.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth aspiration of 18% to 20%; management expects about 60-65% of growth from new client acquisition and the rest from existing clients.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected at 11% to 13%, with management saying this holds for the next couple of years too.
Employee cost growth budgeted at about 13% to 16% in the latest AOP; other expenses to rise about 8% to 9%.
Fuel price increases above roughly 5% are generally passed through to clients, with lags of a few days to a few weeks.
No dividend declared; the board will hold a separate meeting to consider dividend or other ways to enhance shareholder value.
capex_capacity: FY26 vendor partner network of about 20,000 vehicles, versus about 14,000 in FY25; the model remains asset-light.
Over 14% of CCR corporate bookings came through CabDrive Pro, API or the customer app in Q4 FY26.
Direct web booking portal launched in Q4 FY26 for pre-scheduled rides, aimed at premium individuals and SMEs rather than mass B2C.
New core backend platform launched to improve process efficiency.

EV investment remains cautious; capex would rise materially only if EVs become financially sustainable and charging infrastructure and residual values support them. Analyst noted about INR120 million capex over four years (about INR30 million a year).
demand_pricing: Active client base above 1,750; 223 new clients added in FY26 (64 in Q4) versus 188 in FY25.
55% of FY26 revenue from clients associated with ECOS for more than five years. Churn among top 200 clients is about 2-3%, per management.
Demand from GCCs and manufacturing facilities is a notable driver of ETS enterprise wins; CCR growth is diversified across sectors.
Competitive price pressure is mainly in ETS, led by new entrants; management says prices should rise once operations prove unsustainable.

Average revenue per trip fell from about INR1,600 in FY25 to about INR1,550 in FY26, versus about INR1,750-1,780 in FY24. Management cited pricing pressure plus shorter ETS trips and more CCR airport transfers.
No demand impact seen yet from the government's work-from-home appeal.

qa_highlights.question: How is the West Asia crisis affecting demand, and what is FY27 growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: CCR growth slowed in March after the Middle East crisis, with a bounce back expected if the disruption is short. Management aspires to 18-20% growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Can fuel price hikes be passed on, and what is the margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Most contracts have pass-through clauses triggered above roughly 5%, with lags of days to weeks. Management says the 6-7% increase has been fully passed on.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the INR8 crore receivable provision?
qa_highlights.answer: Legal proceedings for recovery are ongoing and management is hopeful. Recovery may come in FY27 or later.

qa_highlights.question: What are the expected growth rates for employee and other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost is budgeted to grow about 13-16% and other expenses about 8-9%, both below the revenue growth target. Management expects operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue per trip declining, and is pricing pressure easing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited ETS pricing pressure and shorter trips plus airport transfers. Pressure appears to have stabilised in the last quarter, while the company is also winning larger enterprise contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins recover to the earlier 14-16% range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 11-13% for FY27 and the next couple of years. It expects CCR brand premium to offset ETS price competition over time.

risks_watch: Margin compression: EBITDA margin in FY26 was about 11.6%, down from roughly 15% at IPO, and Q4 EBITDA fell YoY despite 16.65% revenue growth.
Falling revenue per trip (about INR1,550 in FY26) indicates pricing pressure in ETS from new entrants.
Pending legal recovery of the roughly INR80 million doubtful debt; timing is uncertain.
Middle East and fuel-price volatility affecting CCR demand and the lag in fuel pass-through.
Cost growth versus revenue growth in FY27: the company needs to deliver operating leverage against its 13-16% employee cost budget.
Dividend decision pending a separate board meeting.

Management was candid that pricing pressure in ETS and the March CCR slowdown weighed on the quarter, and it avoided quantifying the timing of margin recovery beyond guidance.

I cannot sacrifice revenue growth for expanding the margin in any one year because then I'm compromising my business for the future.

rows.why: Trips rose about 29% to 5.23 million in FY26 from 4.04 million, 223 new clients were added (64 in Q4), and management targets 18-20% revenue growth with 60-65% from new clients, though the March CCR slowdown and falling revenue per trip temper this.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Asset-light model with about 20,000 vendor vehicles (vs about 14,000 in FY25) and EV capex kept cautious at roughly INR30 million a year; no utilisation figure or board capex plan was disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management only aspires to 18-20% FY27 revenue growth, and margin guidance of 11-13% is below the earlier 14-16% range with ETS price competition still in place.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q4 FY26 EBITDA fell to INR241.5 million from INR264.7 million despite 16.65% revenue growth, and revenue per trip slid to about INR1,550 from about INR1,600, with the Middle East crisis having dented CCR growth in March.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Direct web booking portal launched in Q4 FY26 for pre-scheduled rides and a new core backend platform launched, but no further product launch dates were given.

rows.label: ETS price competition may ease
rows.why: Management says pressure appears to have stabilised in the last quarter and that prices should rise once new entrants' operations prove unsustainable, but revenue per trip still fell to about INR1,550 in FY26 from about INR1,600 in FY25.

rows.label: Recovery of INR80 million doubtful debt
rows.why: Legal recovery proceedings are ongoing and management is hopeful, but the roughly INR80 million provision may only be recovered in FY27 or later, so timing is uncertain.

rows.why: Employee cost is budgeted at 13-16% and other expenses at 8-9% against 18-20% revenue growth, with fuel increases above about 5% passed through to clients with lags of days to weeks.

tone.note: Management was confident on client wins, GCC-driven ETS demand and the CCR brand premium, and cautious on near-term margins, the March CCR slowdown and EV capex. Analysts pressed on margin compression (FY26 about 11.6% vs roughly 15% at IPO), falling revenue per trip and ETS pricing competition.

544239|2026-06.headline: ECOS Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16.7% to INR2,113.7 mn, but EBITDA margin fell to 10.3% and FY27 margin guidance was cut to ~10%.
544239|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 16.7% YoY to INR2,113.72 million and trips rose 27% YoY to about 1.48 million, with 61 new clients added. EBITDA was flat YoY at INR218.47 million, and margin fell to 10.3% from 12.0% a year ago and 11.7% in Q4 FY26. Management attributed the drop to higher operating costs, a higher ETS mix and more intense pricing pressure, especially in ETS. The FY27 EBITDA margin guidance was lowered to around 10% from the earlier 11-13% range, while revenue growth guidance of 15-18% was retained.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said competition and pricing pressure were higher than anticipated, especially in ETS. It has set internal client-level thresholds below which it will not bid, and did not disclose a level; company-wide margin is expected to be held at around 10%.

qa_highlights.question: How will cost savings and productivity be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Automation of CCR contact centre, dispatch, billing and booking, expected mainly to reduce employee expense and improve vehicle utilisation; management said it would also negotiate harder with vendors. Savings were not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the competitive edge given low entry barriers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited three elements: long-standing enterprise relationships, a large reliable vendor supply base built over decades, and processes and people. It said the market is only 15-20% organised.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margins decline and how low can they go?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower rates given to win business are absorbed partly from vendor margins, most evident in ETS. Management declined to specify a floor but said it has internal thresholds.

qa_highlights.question: When and by how much will margins expand?
qa_highlights.answer: No timeline given; management said it is guiding to maintain margins because competition duration is uncertain, with operating leverage expected at a much larger scale (over INR 1,000 crore revenue).

qa_highlights.question: Will ETS and CCR EBITDA margins be disclosed?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said costs are shared across the organisation, so a segment EBITDA split is not practical to provide.

544240|2026-03.headline: Raymond Lifestyle FY26 total income hit record INR7,034 crore (+11% YoY) and EBITDA rose 23% to INR804 crore; Q4 EBITDA up 53% to INR152 crore.
544240|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a recovery year, with record annual total income of INR7,034 crore (+11% YoY) and EBITDA of INR804 crore (11.4% margin, +23%). Q4 FY26 total income was a record INR1,810 crore (+15% YoY), with EBITDA up 53% to INR152 crore and margin up 210 bps QoQ to 8.4%. The company remains debt-free with a net cash surplus of INR179 crore, and net working capital days fell from 87 to 77. Management labelled FY27 a "Year of Consolidation", guiding to double-digit top-line and bottom-line growth without numeric EBITDA guidance.

segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR469 crore (+20% YoY) with double-digit like-for-like growth in retail; EBITDA INR19 crore, 5.4% margin excluding emerging businesses. Core four brands (Park Avenue, ColorPlus, Raymond Ready-to-Wear, Parx) had revenue INR1,667 crore at 7.8% EBITDA margin; emerging businesses are about INR140 crore annual revenue with about INR30 crore loss.

segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR342 crore vs INR248 crore (+38% YoY); EBITDA INR14 crore vs negative INR7 crore, margin 4.1%. March was the highest-ever monthly revenue; US share was about 65-67% and management wants to reduce it.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for Branded Textile profitability, which has declined since FY23?

qa_highlights.question: Working capital levers beyond FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Debtor overdue clamp-down and inventory actions; target below 70 days in FY27, another 8-9 days reduction from 77 days.

qa_highlights.question: Ethnix competitive intensity and growth strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is recalibrating Ethnix toward lighter wedding-guest products such as kurtas and bandis, distribution via TRS and Ethnix stores, and Indo-Western bandhgalas; no numeric growth given.

Factory utilisation rose from a traditional 80-85% to above 90%, with some factories at 95%+, per CEO Satyaki Ghosh.
Store network: about 100 gross EBO additions in FY27 against 50-60 closures, net addition 30-40; network not to dip below 1,653 and expected near 1,700 at end of FY27.
S/4HANA implemented in the textile and home businesses; no store expansion push until strategy work completes, with decision on aggressive expansion closer to end of FY27.
demand_pricing: Q4 FY26 Branded Textile revenue INR831 crore (+14% YoY) on volume growth and premiumisation; management cited ASP growth and mix.

Branded Apparel Q4 revenue INR469 crore (+20% YoY) with double-digit like-for-like growth in retail channels; core four brands INR1,667 crore revenue at 7.8% EBITDA margin, targeted to reach double-digit in about two years.
Emerging and new businesses in Branded Apparel: about INR140 crore annual revenue with about INR30 crore loss; to be reported separately from next quarter.

Garmenting: Q4 revenue INR342 crore (+38% YoY); March was the highest-ever monthly revenue; US share about 65-67%, with a plan to diversify toward Europe and UK after UK FTA and EU FTA; Q1 FY27 order book described as full and Q2 order booking under way.

Gross margin FY26 about 44% including the INR53 crore base-year subsidy; management said Q4 gross margin ex-subsidy would be about 44-45%; Merino wool and flax price increases are a headwind to premiumisation gains.

Working capital days fell from 87 to 77; target below 70 days in FY27.

So, the core brands are actually quite okay at 7.8% and we will endeavour to take it to double-digits over the next two years' time.
As we enter FY '27, we would like to call this the Year of Consolidation.

544240|2026-06.headline: Raymond Lifestyle Q1 FY27 total income rose 6% to INR1,560 crore, EBITDA up 11% to INR135 crore at 8.6% margin, net cash surplus INR154 crore.

Garmenting was the standout, with revenue up 50% to INR296 crore and EBITDA turning positive at INR22 crore. Branded Apparel grew only 4% and Branded Textiles fell about 2%, mainly on base effects and adverse channel and product mix. Management called FY27 a year of consolidation, with net store closures continuing for two to three more quarters, and said Q1 was ahead of budget.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR349 crore, +4% YoY, with LFS and e-commerce growing high double digits (LFS above 25%); EBITDA INR18 crore, margin 5.1% on adverse channel mix.

guidance_outlook: Management is bullish on FY27 and said Q1 is ahead of budget phasing and ahead of last year; Q2 described as decent.
Garmenting capacity is full through December; orders booked from January onwards. Management said no risk to margins on cost-plus contracts, though changes in Sep-Oct could affect pricing.
Price hikes to start in Q2: management estimates 5-7% in apparel and 7-9% in fabric, calibrated against volumes.

Medium term: aim to at least double turnover in five years and grow EBITDA faster than revenue, before any Kearney-led transformation outcomes. Mid-teens ROCE described as the endeavour, not a target. Garmenting EBITDA double-digit described as an endeavour with no firm timeline.
Net branded EBO openings to be negative in FY27; EBO closures expected to take another 2-3 quarters.

Ethnix plan: shift sherwanis and bandhgalas above INR50,000 to made-to-measure; basic kurtas to be sold through TRS and e-commerce; high-impact flagship stores in wedding areas.
demand_pricing: Garmenting US share fell to 55% under tariffs and has recovered to 59-60%; UK rose from 10% to 12% and Europe from 6% to 7-8%. Management aims to bring US to about 55%.

Branded apparel: management attributed the weak quarter to Adhik Maas (about one month without auspicious buying) and delayed festive dates by 20-25 days. Casual brands (ColorPlus, Parx) growing double digit; casual share in Park Avenue and Raymond Ready-to-Wear reached about 18%.
Retail: TRS stores up 5-6% and EBOs up 3% like-for-like. Management said premium-end off-take in Q1 was not an issue.
Raw material inflation YoY: wool about +100%, cotton and flax about +20%, chemicals about +30%. Gross margin was held despite this because Q1 sold at forward-booked prices.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited wool, flax, cotton, dyes and chemicals as rising costs. Mitigation includes new vendors, Make in India sourcing, freight consolidation, and a cost transformation project. Price increases to begin in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Garmenting outlook and whether contracts allow pass-through of RM costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders are cost-plus, and bookings for January onward are open with December capacity full. Higher plant utilisation is expected to help margins. Management declined to give firm double-digit EBITDA guidance, citing unpredictable international trade conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Depreciation rise of about 25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR11 crore was a one-time lease-accounting error from last year and will not recur, so it can be excluded from run-rate depreciation.

qa_highlights.question: Store rationalisation timeline and Ethnix store additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Closures will take another 2-3 quarters, so FY27 net branded EBO openings will be negative. Ethnix will shift top-end products to made-to-measure and move basic lines to TRS and e-commerce, with flagship stores in wedding areas.

qa_highlights.question: Medium-term revenue, margin and ROCE targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to at least double turnover and grow EBITDA faster than revenue in five years, before any Kearney-led project outcomes. Mid-teens ROCE is described as a good outcome for a manufacturing business, not a target.

qa_highlights.answer: Branded apparel grew 4% due to EBO closures, with e-commerce and LFS growing high double digits. Order books span Europe, US, Japan, Korea and Asia. Management said FY28 is not being looked at closely.

544240|2026-09.headline: Raymond Lifestyle Q2 FY27 total income rose 14% YoY to INR2,125 crore, a record, with EBITDA up 4% to INR270 crore and margin down to 12.7%.
544240|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 set a record quarterly total income of INR2,125 crore (up 14% YoY), with revenue from operations at INR2,075 crore (up 13%). Consolidated EBITDA rose 4% YoY to INR270 crore, but margin fell about 120 bps to 12.7% on freight, wool and cotton costs and higher brand spend ahead of the festive season. The company ended with a net cash surplus of INR69 crore versus a net debt of INR246 crore a year earlier, and working capital days fell to 82 from 105. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of double-digit revenue growth, mid-to-high double-digit EBITDA growth, INR300 crore-plus net cash and double-digit PBT growth, with H2 expected to carry the year.

qa_highlights.question: Is Branded Apparel's strong growth driven by channel stocking from the festive shift or by secondary sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Diwali timing moved about 20-25 days; Q2 had only partial primary loading, yet Branded Apparel grew 20%, backed by secondary offtake and like-to-like store growth in double digits.

qa_highlights.question: How will Branded Apparel margins move, and what is the medium-term target?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin of 8.8% held despite higher marketing and raw material costs; management expects improvement from fresh pricing and scale, guiding to double-digit-plus margin in a couple of years.

qa_highlights.question: How will H2 deliver the FY27 guidance given H1 revenue up about 10% and EBITDA up mid-single digit?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 is seasonally larger (about 57-58% of revenue); with Diwali in November, management expects H2 revenue growth above 10% and H2 EBITDA margin above 12.7%, with cost-saving initiatives and full price pass-through in Q3-Q4.

544248|2026-06.headline: Mach Travel Q1 FY27 revenue rose 538% YoY to INR144.33 crore, with EBITDA margin compressing to 6.09% from 7.17%.

544252|2026-03.headline: Bajaj Housing Finance Q4 FY26 PAT rose 14% to INR669 crore (20% ex one-time tax benefit), with AUM up 23% and GNPA steady at 27 bps.
544252|2026-03.overview: AUM crossed INR140,000 crore, growing 23% YoY, with quarterly AUM additions of INR7,294 crore and disbursements up 23% YoY to INR17,506 crore. Spreads compressed 10 bps QoQ to 1.7% and NIM fell 12 bps to 3.8% on lower acquisition yields and a 15 bps PLR pass-through in December. Asset quality held (GNPA 27 bps, NNPA 11 bps), but annualised credit cost rose to 19 bps from 11 bps YoY on a deliberate Stage 2 provision top-up. Management guided to ROA compression of about 10 bps in FY27 (towards upper end of the 2.0-2.2% medium-term range) assuming no policy rate change, and said it will firm up guidance with Q1 results.

544252|2026-06.headline: Bajaj Housing Q1 FY27: record AUM addition of INR8,918 crore (AUM up 24% to INR1.496 lakh crore) and PAT up 23% to INR715 crore, but NIM fell 14 bps to 3.7%.
544252|2026-06.overview: Disbursements rose 33% YoY to INR19,509 crore, a record quarter, and AUM grew 24% to INR1.496 lakh crore. PAT grew 23% YoY to INR715 crore, with ROA stable at 2.3% and ROE up to 12.5%. Net margin compressed 14 bps QoQ to 3.7% as portfolio yield fell, while cost of funds eased 7 bps to 7.2%. Q1 credit cost of 5 bps was flattered by a one-off assignment of about INR2,300 crore, and management guided FY27 NIM down 20-25 bps and credit cost at 10-15 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the 20-25 bps FY27 NIM compression, and is there any pricing relief or PLR hike possibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the compression mainly to yield decline: high-yield book is running off while new business comes in at lower yields in a stable rate regime. Acquisition pricing has been stable, and no large-scale upward pricing move is assumed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 credit cost drop to 5 bps? Are there one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, two one-offs: a Q4 FY26 Stage 2 provision build that was not repeated, and a roughly INR2,300 crore assignment that released Stage 1 provisions. Management said to treat it as about 5 bps; the FY27 guide stays at 10-15 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NIM fall 13-14 bps when spreads were flat and cost of funds fell 7 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: The spread is computed on period-end portfolio yield versus average cost of funds, so it moved only 3-4 bps. The margin decline is from portfolio yield compression, which will continue through FY27 and offset the cost-of-funds benefit.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of funds outlook for Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of funds is expected to be sideways in Q2 FY27 with a downward bias, helped by hedging, repayment of older high-cost borrowings and resets of some older borrowings to lower rates.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the LAP and DF Stage 2 to Stage 3 movement not raising provisions, and is there stress in LAP?
qa_highlights.answer: LAP provisions are formula-based on DPD, so roll-backs and roll-ins net off; the LAP movement was INR18 crore in total, not one account. DF provisioning was already held at 48-49% on the account. Management cited LAP GNPA in a 46-76 bps range over seven quarters and said there is no segment or geography concern.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Stage 1 provisions stay flat despite a INR7,500 crore rise in Stage 1 assets?
qa_highlights.answer: The annual January ECL recalibration lowered Stage 1 rates on most portfolios because credit performance was stronger, and the mix of new and attrited customers also shifted. Management said there is no simple pool-to-pool calculation.

544253|2026-03.headline: Kross Q4 FY26 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 225.4 crore, with EBITDA margin at 14.9%; management guides 14-15% margins and FY27 growth near 22%.
544253|2026-03.overview: Kross closed FY26 with revenue of INR 673.2 crore (+8.5%) and PAT of INR 55.2 crore (8.2% margin), after a slow H1 and a stronger H2 (H2 revenue 49.2% above H1). Q4 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 225.4 crore, EBITDA rose 25% to INR 33.6 crore and PAT rose 31% to INR 22.4 crore. Management says the Middle East conflict caused LPG shortages and commodity and consumable cost increases in Q4, with steel price hikes of INR 3-5/kg expected from April and a retrospective OEM pass-through lagging by about one quarter. The company has raised prices about 5% in trailer axles and suspensions and says it has fully deployed IPO proceeds.

Gains from the unhedged portion: INR7.4 crore in Q4 FY25, INR45 crore in Q3 FY26, INR20 crore in Q4 FY26.
Management says the import duty and the advance authorisation scheme do not apply to its domestic business; the duty is passed to consumers.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the customs duty hike and advance authorisation on sales and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the advance authorisation targets exporters, so it does not apply. The duty is passed to consumers, with no margin impact; it may shift demand from bars and coins toward exchanging old gold for jewellery.

qa_highlights.question: Hedging levels for FY26 and the FY27 plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Hedging was 57% in Q4 FY25, 63% in Q3 FY26 and 67% in Q4 FY26, averaging about 60% for FY26. The target is 75-80% in FY27, held back by MCX margin and premium costs of 15-20% that tied up cash.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 revenue guidance raised from INR12,000 crore to INR13,500 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 beat the INR9,500 crore guidance by about INR1,000 crore. Management cites non-Maharashtra demand (about 10% of business) and strong same-store growth, which pushed the range up to INR13,500 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why are the margin drivers one-off rather than structural, given likely repeat discounts and franchise growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the discounts were one-time events worth about 0.5% of Q4 sales. Bars and coins (40% of Q4 sales) drove most of the dip, and it expects that mix to normalise to about 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin split between bars and coins and jewellery?
qa_highlights.answer: Bars and coins earn 0.5-1% gross margin; plain gold jewellery earns 12.5-13%. Franchise gross margin is about 2-3%, nearly net margin since the franchisee bears all costs.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory turnover decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes the 3.8x FY26 turnover to about 8 COCO stores opened in Q4 that have not matured. It says turnover has been broadly flat, declining slightly over two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 store additions and non-Maharashtra plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Plan of 25 stores: 5-7 COCO and the balance FOCO, mostly outside Maharashtra (UP, Bihar, MP, Gujarat, Gurgaon). Demand for franchises is strong and under evaluation.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year bars and coins share and promoter shareholding timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Bars and coins were about 32% of FY26 sales. The promoter must reach 75% by September 2027, three years after the September 2024 listing.

Franchise mix rising (FOCO margins about 2-3%) could weigh on gross margin as the network expands.
Inventory turnover fell to 3.8x as new stores ramp; the new-market ramp needs watching.

544256|2026-06.headline: PNG Jewellers Q1 FY27 revenue rose 41% YoY to INR2,413 crore, with EBITDA up 57% to INR192.4 crore and PAT up 52% to INR105.3 crore.

EBITDA margin expanded 80 bps to 8.0% and PAT margin rose 40 bps to 4.4%, with gross margin flat at 13.2% reported. Management kept FY27 guidance (around 25 store additions to 103 stores, about 7% EBITDA margin, about INR400 crore other expenses) and flagged that Q1 other expenses were low due to cuts in marketing and no store launches. Hedging gains and lower other income were discussed in detail, and the promoter stake and franchise economics drew scrutiny.

segments.commentary: Grew 8% YoY; management attributed the slowdown to B2B billing timing and stock replenishment, with franchise openings expected to pick up in Q2-Q3 (about 10 legacy and 5 litestyle planned).

qa_highlights.question: Why is gross margin flat YoY despite mix shift toward retail, and what is the ideal retail margin at a 10-11% studded ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: Reported gross margin is flat because hedging gains are shown separately; ex-hedging adjusted gross margin is up about 40-50 bps YoY. Management targets 12.5-13.5% retail margin at a 10-11% studded ratio, and 13-14% overall retail gross margin including hedging gains.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses grow only about 5% despite store expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited conservative spending amid demand uncertainty, lower scheme-redemption discounts, marketing kept within 1.5% of sales with 250-300 hoardings cut, and no store launches in Q1. Spending will rise in Q3-Q4 with expansion, but EBITDA guidance is still expected to be met.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 other expense guidance and why was other income so different between Q4 and Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses are guided at about 3% of sales, roughly INR400 crore for FY27. Other income was about INR10 crore in Q1 versus about INR12 crore in Q4 per the CFO, who said lower fixed deposits placed on mortgage drove the decline; cash and hedging margin money also hold some balances.

qa_highlights.question: What is the store expansion and COCO/FOCO mix plan through FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Plan adds 25 stores in FY27 to reach 103 (63 COCO, balance FOCO), then 37 each in FY28 and FY29 to reach 140 and 177. By March 2029, about 75 COCO and 40 FOCO, with 113 legacy and 64 litestyle stores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin trajectory and hedging plan?
qa_highlights.answer: PAT margin underlying ex-hedging is targeted at 4.1-4.25% in FY27 per the CFO, versus about 4.2% per the CEO; 4.5-4.7% by FY29. Hedging is about 70%+ now, targeted at about 80% around Q3 FY27 and fully hedged in FY28. Hedging gains were about INR45 crore in Q3 FY26, INR20 crore in Q4 FY26 and INR5.5-6 crore in Q2 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How is Litestyle progressing on studded mix, gross margin and store count?
qa_highlights.answer: Studded ratio is about 32.9-34% now, targeted at about 50% in a couple of years. Current litestyle gross margin is about 18-20%, versus 30-35% for the format once studded mix rises. Litestyle store target is 65-70 by March 2029 and about 100 over the longer term.

qa_highlights.question: Why are franchise revenue growth (8%) and e-commerce growth lower than company-operated stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Franchise sales are booked as B2B, so initial stocking and replenishment timing affect quarterly numbers; management expects franchise openings to pick up in Q2-Q3 (about 10 legacy and 5 litestyle). E-commerce is deliberately shifting mix away from bars and coins toward jewellery, so margins should improve but total sales growth may slow.

544256|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR2,666 crore and EBITDA 57% to INR224.6 crore, with margin up 186 bps to 8.4%.
544256|2026-09.overview: P N Gadgil reported Q2 FY27 revenue of about INR2,660-2,666 crore (up 22% YoY), EBITDA of INR224.6 crore (8.4% margin) and PAT of INR121.1 crore (4.5% margin), with profit growing roughly twice as fast as revenue. Retail grew 31% with SSSG of 25.5%, while e-commerce fell 84% after the company cut low-margin coin sales. Management said about INR200 crore of Navaratri sales shifted from Q2 into Q3 this year, and the company completed the Silvostyle acquisition on 1 October. Gross margin was down 50 bps QoQ, which management attributed to franchisee share rising to 17% from 12%.

qa_highlights.answer: Navaratri moved from Q2 last year into Q3 this year; about INR200 crore of revenue from the 10 days shifted. The 50 bps QoQ gross margin dip was attributed to franchisee mix rising to 17% from 12%.

qa_highlights.question: How will capital be allocated across franchise, COCO and new brands?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 is FOCO-led in Q3-Q4; from FY28 the split is 50-50 COCO/FOCO for both legacy and YOOU. Internal accruals are expected to fund COCO expansion, and debt is to fall 20-25% by 2030.

qa_highlights.question: How mature stores in UP are performing (turns, stud ratio, margin)?
qa_highlights.answer: Stock turn is about 1.1x (plan was 1x), revenue about INR60 crore per store (plan INR50-55 crore), stud ratio above 17% (plan 15%), gross margin about 35%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path for YOOU inventory turn and why did legacy turn fall to 3.7x?
qa_highlights.answer: YOOU is about 70% diamond and 30% gold, with a target of 1.8-2x turns at maturity against 0.8x now. Management said legacy turns of 3.7-4x are well above the 2-2.5x industry norm and are sustainable as new stores mature.

qa_highlights.answer: Part of the INR700 crore QIP went into festive working capital; the rest is in FDs (about INR1,191 crore, up INR637 crore QoQ). Gross borrowings rose about INR385 crore since March on GML loans, but net borrowings fell INR167 crore after collateral and FDs.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for employee cost and other expenses in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost fell about INR6 crore QoQ on lower variable pay. Other expenses were INR86 crore in Q2 versus INR85 crore in Q1, and management expects similar moderation in H2.

544258|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 4% QoQ to INR496 crore, but EBITDA margin slipped to 5.0% as Middle East crisis cut EXIM volumes 11% QoQ.
544258|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew about 4% QoQ to INR496 crore, the fourth straight quarter of sequential growth. EBITDA fell from INR27 crore to INR25 crore, with margin down from 5.6% to 5.0%, and PAT dropped from INR10.8 crore to INR8.3 crore. Total containers handled were 57,754, up 4.3% YoY but down 7% QoQ, with EXIM down 10.96% QoQ and domestic almost flat. For FY26, containers rose 6.14% to 2,26,578, and management attributed the shortfall from double-digit growth to the March disruption from the Strait of Hormuz closure.

financial_highlights.change: +4% QoQ from INR478 crore in Q3
down from INR27 crore in Q3
down from INR10.8 crore in Q3; margin 1.7% vs 2.3%

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 23,350 containers, up 17.79% YoY and down less than 1% QoQ, helped by pivots to chemicals, FMCG, aggregates and salt. FY26 volume 86,353, up 8.16% YoY.

segments.name: Devaliya MMCT (Morbi)
segments.commentary: 32-acre multimodal terminal now fully operational. Tiles throughput fell sharply in March due to propane and natural gas shortages affecting about 700 units; volumes are rising month-on-month in industrial chemicals.

capex_capacity: FY26 capex was over INR70 crore (about INR74 crore per Q&A), spent on specialised containers, reach stackers, commercial vehicles and handling equipment.

Own specialised container fleet is over 1,000 units.

demand_pricing: Management says the order book is strong, with pedigreed customers for the rest of the year, and that the East Coast EXIM pipeline is robust.
