Capacity on US and Europe routes is about 30-35% of normal; Cape of Good Hope diversions add about 3,500 nautical miles and 10-15 days.
Realisations were hit by geopolitical factors and are expected to improve as EXIM volumes recover.

Receivables have risen, with the company citing growth in retail MMCT customers (up 25-30% YoY) who pay only when the next consignment ships. Management said the company had INR600+ crore in receivables, a figure raised by an analyst and not disputed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did debt rise from INR172 crore to INR217 crore despite IPO net proceeds of about INR363 crore, of which about INR163 crore went to debt repayment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rise reflects working capital needs as the new Devaliya MMCT became operational.

qa_highlights.question: Can you give a revenue split between rail, road and water?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split revenue, saying it operates as a consolidated multimodal logistics provider and that splitting would distort the picture.

qa_highlights.question: Why are receivables rising and when will cash flow turn positive, given negative operating cash flow in FY25 and FY26 and a planned INR100 crore capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets debtor days below 120 this year, says INR100 crore of IPO funds is still unspent, and expects realisations and cash flow to improve as EXIM recovers. It said the EXIM trade should improve within the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What further margin pressure is coming from April pricing, and when will margins recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give numerical guidance, but said margins should improve sequentially, with EBITDA margin targeted back toward 7%.

qa_highlights.question: Where will the INR100 crore capex go and what are the domestic growth drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex covers specialised containers, commercial vehicles and heavy equipment. Domestic growth is expected to come from the Morbi MMLP, tiles volumes once propane supply returns, and Western seaboard clients.

qa_highlights.question: What are the drivers of the ROE/ROCE decline and the outlook for the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects ROE and ROCE to return to strong double-digit levels as margins recover from 4.6-4.7%, citing a debt position it considers under control.

544258|2026-06.headline: Western Carriers Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR465 crores, with PAT of about INR9 crores and domestic TEUs up 37%.
544258|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew about 12% YoY to INR465 crores from INR416 crores, with EBITDA of about INR19 crores (4.1% margin) and PAT of about INR9 crores, up about 13% QoQ. Total container throughput of 58,261 TEUs beat Q4 FY26 (57,754) for the first time, driven by domestic volumes up 37% YoY while EXIM grew only 3.2%. Management attributed EXIM weakness to Middle East war-linked vessel disruption and freight rate spikes, and said working capital days fell from 120 to about 111 and debt declined from INR217 crores to about INR197 crores since March. Analysts pressed on the lack of price pass-through, weak cash generation and receivables; management did not commit to a price hike.

financial_highlights.change: +13% QoQ vs INR8 crores in Q4 FY26; PAT margin 1.9% vs 1.7%
down from 139 (Q4); management also cited 142 days in an analyst question
down from INR217 crores at March 2026

segments.commentary: Domestic TEUs 23,909 (+37% YoY); domestic now about 40% of mix vs under 30% earlier, and DSO about 40% of top line vs under 25% two-three years ago. Company ordered 150 further specialised 40-ft containers: 50 delivered, 100 due this quarter.

segments.name: EXIM
segments.commentary: EXIM TEUs 34,352 (+3.2% YoY). Freight on US and European routes reportedly rose 3-4x in recent months, with some routes near USD9,000/TEU vs USD3,000/TEU a few months earlier; management described EXIM as muted for four to five quarters.

demand_pricing: Domestic demand strong: TEUs up 37% YoY, supported by specialised containers and existing EXIM customers expanding into domestic.
EXIM disrupted by congestion at JNPT (about 30,000 TEU backlog), Cape of Good Hope routing adding about 15 days to US East Coast voyages, and war-risk and bunker surcharges.
Most contracts are long-term (three to four years) with some flexibility; management did not confirm any fixed-price exposure or price hike plans when asked directly.
Management said margin pressure stems from erratic vessel schedules that make cargo flow non-linear, and that the company is absorbing part of the EXIM cost impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why can the company not pass on higher container rates through price hikes; is it locked into fixed-price contracts causing margin pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most contracts are three- to four-year and have some flexibility, but disruptions make cargo flow non-linear, causing margin hits at both import and export ends. It expects EXIM volumes to recover strongly once sea freight eases, and said it is learning to live with disruption.

qa_highlights.question: Why not wait for a price hike and instead keep insulating customers from volatility, given rising working capital days and low ROE?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed the premise that it is subsidising customers, citing working capital days down from 120 to about 111 and quarterly operating cash flow of about INR13 crores versus INR9.2 crores in Q4. It said it pivoted to domestic and streamlined operations rather than waiting for peace.

qa_highlights.question: Why are debtor days not easing and why not collect more from customers to protect cash and leverage, with capex to stay elevated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debtor days fell from 139 to about 135 and debt declined from INR217 crores to about INR197 crores since March. It said it is pushing customers and SME collections and that a rise to INR1,000 crores would only come with roughly ten times growth.

qa_highlights.question: What return thresholds guide capex and when will investments become earnings accretive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the first criterion is ensuring customer supply chains can run, with the remainder targeting a healthy double-digit return across specialised containers, heavy equipment and commercial vehicles. No formal benchmark or payback timeline was given.

risks_watch: EXIM volume and freight: EXIM grew only 3.2% YoY and remains exposed to Middle East war, vessel schedule disruption and freight rates; a prolonged war would prolong this.
Margin: EBITDA margin of 4.1% and PAT margin of 1.9%; management did not show price pass-through and analysts flagged low ROE (below 5%, per an analyst).

Working capital and receivables: debtor days (about 135 per management, 142 per an analyst) and working capital days (about 111) remain high; cumulative operating cash flow over six years was cited by an analyst as negative INR43 crores (not disputed by management).
Capex of about INR100 crores against debt of about INR197 crores; funding and leverage are open questions.
Next quarter: confirm delivery of 100 specialised containers, progress of the new large domestic projects, and whether working capital days keep falling.

544260|2026-03.headline: Northern Arc posted record Q4FY26 PAT of INR133 crore (up 251% YoY) and FY26 PAT of INR406 crore, with AUM at INR16,594 crore (up 22% YoY).
544260|2026-03.overview: Northern Arc reported its highest-ever quarterly profit of INR133 crore in Q4FY26, taking FY26 PAT to INR406 crore (up 33% YoY). AUM grew 22% YoY and 10% QoQ to INR16,594 crore, with direct-to-customer (D2C) at 59% of AUM. Credit cost fell to 2.2% in Q4 (from 3.5% in Q3) and 2.8% for FY26, helped by the RBI's FLDG-related ECL clarification, which management said contributed a one-off benefit. Management guided FY27 AUM growth of 22-25% and ROA above 3%, with ROE in the mid-to-late teens over 8-10 quarters.

segments.commentary: AUM above INR5,000 crore, growing about 50% in the year per analyst; 70% repeat customers; risk-adjusted yield targeted at 15-16%; ROA stated as upward of about 4%. Short-tenure book reduced to near zero, and an APR cap introduced.

segments.name: MSME (incl. LAP)
segments.commentary: Portfolio INR3,691 crore, up about 43% YoY, with 17 new branches in FY26. X-bucket collection efficiency 99.4% in March 2026; average ticket INR11-15 lakh; yield 17-18%.

segments.commentary: AUM INR1,009 crore (+8% QoQ); record quarterly disbursement about INR305 crore (+17% QoQ); 64 branches added, network about 342; X-bucket collection efficiency 99.6%. MFI is 6% of AUM; 84% of MFI book covered under CGFMU.

segments.commentary: FY26 placement volume INR11,834 crore with placement fee income up 22% YoY to INR31 crore; credit fund AUM INR3,092 crore earning about INR38 crore fee in FY26. Securitisation placed about INR10,000 crore last year.

qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 22-25% AUM growth (about 3x GDP) and a 3%+ ROA target, with mid-to-late teens ROE in 8-10 quarters.

qa_highlights.answer: Consumer finance is underwritten via scorecards with a 15% risk-adjusted return; MSME average ticket is INR11-15 lakh, yield 17-18%, all with 100% registered mortgage. Management acknowledged the small base inflates growth rates.

qa_highlights.question: Why has ECL coverage fallen, particularly Stage 2 and Stage 3?
qa_highlights.answer: The RBI FLDG clarification (Feb 2026) let the company count FLDG cover in ECL; over 50% of Stage 2 is FLDG-covered. Stage 3 is now mainly secured MSME, given 100% write-off of unsecured loans at 90 DPD.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FLDG reversal one-off, and what is the underlying Q4 credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Q4 FLDG benefit was INR29 crore and the INR66 crore overlay is prudence. Adjusting for prior-year provision, the underlying Q4 credit cost would have been about INR120 crore (about 2.9-3%), with 2.7-2.8% as steady state.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for cost of funds and NIM given rate movements?
qa_highlights.answer: Fixed-rate share rose from about 30% to 40%; incremental CoF 8.7% vs 9.3%; management expects to hold 8.5-8.6% and NIM to expand as D2C mix rises to 65%. Management expects RBI rate increases in the next couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said yield is 15-16% risk-adjusted; short-tenure book cut to near zero; APR cap introduced; no partner concentration figure given in the call.

qa_highlights.answer: Bank borrowings fell from about 65% of total in March 2025 to about 52% in March 2026, with more offshore, capital market and securitisation (PTC) funding.

544261|2026-03.headline: Arkade posted record Q4 FY26 pre-sales of Rs 303 crore (+40% YoY), but FY26 PAT fell to Rs 5 crore after a Rs 182 crore Filmistan tenancy-rights write-off.

544263|2026-03.headline: KRN Heat Exchanger FY26 standalone total income rose 57.36% to Rs.689.95 crore; Q4 standalone net profit up 22.69% to Rs.16.87 crore.
544263|2026-03.overview: FY26 standalone total income grew 57.36% YoY to Rs.689.95 crore, with EBITDA up 19.41% to Rs.84.79 crore and net profit up 42.11% to Rs.71.31 crore. Consolidated FY26 total income was Rs.609.81 crore (+38.06%), EBITDA Rs.112.48 crore (+59.52%) and net profit Rs.76.47 crore (+44.62%). Q4 consolidated EBITDA rose 77.56% to Rs.33.55 crore, while Q4 standalone total income rose 55.06% to Rs.204.93 crore. Management said the new Neemrana HVAC facility is still ramping up, with working capital building in inventory and receivables, and a board-approved enabling fund raise of up to Rs.500 crore whose objective is not yet finalised.

financial_highlights.value: Around 3x YoY (per analyst question, not disputed)

segments.name: Heat exchangers (fin and tube, KRN Heat Exchanger)
segments.commentary: Management said the old facility was fully utilised in FY26; fin and tube still accounts for about 95% of revenue, with other products about 5%. Fin and tube growth expected above 80-90%, mainly from data centres.

segments.name: HVAC / new facility (KRN HVAC Products)
segments.commentary: Utilisation of the new facility was about 15% in FY26 for HVAC. Management targets 50% in FY27 and 80% in FY28 across about eight new products and new geometries.

segments.name: Data centre
segments.commentary: Data centre was about 16% of revenue in FY26 per one answer and about 18.7-19% in Q4 per another answer; management expects this to rise quarter on quarter. Top-10 customers include three data centre customers.

segments.name: Bus AC
segments.commentary: Bus AC revenue was about Rs.10 crore in FY26; management targets at least 15% market share in FY27 and has a Rs.150 crore revenue target shown in the presentation, with two to three OEMs onboarded.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export was about Rs.100 crore in FY26 and management aims for roughly double in FY27; export order book is about Rs.120 crore including data centre orders. Geographies cited: UAE, US/North America and Europe.

segments.name: Railways / refrigeration
segments.commentary: Bar and plate heat exchanger approved by Indian Railways for field trial; company says it was L1 in three recent tenders. Full HVAC system for railways needs about 6-8 months of approvals, so limited FY27 contribution expected.

guidance_outlook: New facility utilisation targets: about 50% in FY27 and about 80% in FY28; old facility to stay fully utilised.
Management expects next eight quarters to be the highest ever, with Q4 described as an average quarter and quarter-on-quarter improvement expected.
Export to roughly double in FY27 versus about Rs.100 crore in FY26.

Margins expected to improve slightly, helped by a 5% PLI benefit in FY26, a likely RIFS state incentive of about 1.56% of top line for 10 years on the new facility, export mix and solar power savings, offset by higher depreciation and overheads.
Inventory expected to come under control within about three quarters; minimum six months to normalise per management.
Analyst cited a Rs.2,250-2,850 crore revenue target; management did not confirm the target or its timing.
capex_capacity: New Neemrana facility inaugurated 11 March 2026; production commissioning began May 2025 and the plant was shifted to fully in the week before the call.

Current facility is fully commissioned; about eight new products added, including WOT condenser, roll-bond evaporator, frost-free evaporator, skin condenser, bar and plate, dry air cooler, ammonia evaporator and bus AC, plus new fin geometries.
Further capex on existing facility is about Rs.30-40 crore over the next two years, mainly for line balancing for data centre geometry, per management's rough estimate.
Micro-channel (MCHX) product expected by end 2026 or early 2027; plate-and-plate heat exchanger (CDU) under study for next year.
Solar plant installed and operational.
demand_pricing: Raw material pass-through: management said copper LME, aluminium LME and USD-INR changes are passed to customers on a quarterly basis, with freight and logistics also passed through; it said close to 100% pass-through is possible.
UAE dispatches were disrupted in March 2026 due to the geopolitical situation; dispatches restarted in May 2026. Freight costs rose and are being passed on.
North America and Europe dispatches unaffected per management; Europe is early-stage and North America is larger than Europe for data centre exports.
Company says it competes with European and North American suppliers, not Chinese players, given customised, low-volume products.
Data centre demand: some Indian customers issue one-month firm orders on a rolling basis; one long-lead customer booked six to seven months.
Vertiv vendor approval received after QA audit; billing expected to start in coming weeks or months; Schneider Electric is the biggest domestic data centre customer.

qa_highlights.question: Are new products for liquid-cooled AI data centres in development?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said liquid cooling is early in India; fin and tube remains the core product for chillers and dry coolers, with micro-channel due by end 2026 or early 2027 and plate heat exchanger for CDUs under study.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company pass raw material costs to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management said copper, aluminium and USD-INR movements are passed through quarter on quarter and close to 100% can be passed on under current contracts; there is a one-quarter lag.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory up about 3x and receivables up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited about Rs.15-20 crore of UAE material held after March dispatch was blocked, about Rs.8 crore of export dispatched in March but not billed, minimum stock for new products, BIS-related pre-buying of inner groove tube, and new customer onboarding. Normalisation expected in about six months, with inventory days around two and a half months currently.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise equity when internal cash flow may suffice?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the IPO proceeds were exceeded by investment in the current facility and working capital will be short; the board approved an enabling resolution up to Rs.500 crore, with objectives not yet concluded. Bank funding is also an option.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 revenue share from products other than fin and tube?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have the figure on the call; it said non-fin-and-tube business is about 5% of revenue overall.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bus AC Rs.150 crore target backed by orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said two to three OEMs have been onboarded and regular supply has started, with about 15% market share targeted; no specific Rs.150 crore order book was quantified.

risks_watch: Working capital and receivables build-up; inventory normalisation timeline (about six months) and the Rs.500 crore equity raise, whose use is unconfirmed.
BIS certification issue on inner groove tube (deadline around 20-28 May 2026) could drive imports and inventory build-up.
Copper and aluminium price volatility in recent weeks, which management said is beyond expectation; pass-through has a one-quarter lag.
Geopolitical disruption to UAE dispatches and freight costs.
Ramp-up pace of the new facility versus 50%/80% utilisation targets; Q4 incremental revenue from the new facility was about Rs.15-16 crore per an analyst's estimate.
Concentration of data centre revenue (about 16-19%) and dependence on a few large customers such as Schneider Electric.
Depreciation and overhead rising ahead of revenue.
544263|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth, data centre demand and utilisation targets, but evasive on the Rs.500 crore fund raise, the Rs.120 crore UAE order, the Q4 non-fin-and-tube share and the specific data centre order book. Several answers were vague or deferred to later updates.

So, now we have eight new businesses, so that is also we have to build the inventory.
Of course, slight improvement will be there, but honestly in the last two, three weeks in this copper and aluminum silver price is beyond the expectation because they sharply increase.

544264|2026-03.headline: Diffusion Engineers Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 38.08% YoY to INR1,415.74 million, with FY27 revenue growth guided above 20%.
544264|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue was INR1,415.74 million (+38.08% YoY) and EBITDA excluding other income was INR206.89 million (+39.96%), at a 14.61% margin. Consolidated FY26 revenue was INR4,066.28 million (+21.28%) with PAT of INR504.1 million (+39.87%). Standalone growth was weaker: Q4 revenue +12.18% and Q4 PAT down 3.05%, which management attributed to capacity constraints in wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering running at about 85-90% utilisation. Order book stood at about INR200 crores as of 30 April 2026, up from about INR100 crores a year earlier. New Unit 4 capacity is being commissioned from Q1 FY27 onward.

segments.name: Welding consumables (products)
segments.commentary: Management cited roughly 30% of revenue; under 3% (said 2-3%) of the business is conventional, with the rest special hard-facing and repair electrodes. Wires line at 85-90% utilisation; new wire line expected July 2026.

segments.name: Wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering
segments.commentary: Cited at roughly 30% of revenue combined with heavy engineering; running at 85-90% utilisation, and expected to grow faster than consumables. Roller-press rolls, steel mill rollers and VRM rollers are cited as growth areas; first VRM order won.

segments.name: Services
segments.commentary: Roughly 10% of revenue per management. Covers on-site breakdown repair, hot kiln alignment and bulk deposition, with about 50-60 welding technicians deployed. UAE subsidiary set up for service and overlay work is now operational and expected to contribute from FY27.

segments.name: Railways (developmental)
segments.commentary: L1 in multiple contracts and some letters of intent received for Vande Bharat ecosystem components; execution 6-9 months, with substantial revenue expected from next year at likely lower initial margins.

segments.name: Defence (Tejorup Sunmay Systems)
segments.commentary: Investment made in February 2026 for VSHORADS work; still in prototype stage with a DRDO sanction order for 200 launchers and 1,200 rockets. No revenue expected in FY26 or in FY27 in any significant amount.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth expected to be more than 20%, supported by capacity additions, order inflows and higher-margin engineered products.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected to rise by about 80-100 basis points, aided by operating leverage and cost consolidation; gross margin may come under pressure from raw material volatility.
Medium-term aspiration of INR650 crore-plus revenue at 15-16% EBITDA margin, expected to be reached in under 3 years (2-3 years on annual run-rate basis).

Capex of about INR100 crores from IPO proceeds (INR70 crores for wear part/plate/heavy engineering, INR30 crores for electrode and slitting facility) is expected to support INR800-900 crores revenue; no additional capex planned for INR650 crores.
Debtor days targeted at 80-85 for FY27 and inventory days at 60-65; FY26 debtor days were 98 and inventory days 66.
International revenue share expected to rise to about 15%, with international sales growing above 20%.
capex_capacity: New 10 tons-per-day electrode plant commissioned around November-December 2025, along with an in-house strip-slitting line for flux-cored wires.
Wear plate capacity expanded by about 25% and now commissioned.

Unit 4 (about 170,000-180,000 sq ft) for wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering: partial utilisation from May 2026, most capacity live by end of Q1 FY27 (quarter ending June 2026), with the facility expected to be fully commissioned by end of Q1 2027 per management.
Current utilisation: wires about 85-90%; wear plates and heavy engineering about 85-90%. Management expects utilisation to fall to roughly 50-60% once new shop floors are live.
New wire line expected to be delivered in July 2026.
demand_pricing: Order book about INR200 crores as of 30 April 2026, up from about INR100 crores on 31 March 2025; management expects 80-90% to execute in FY27, with staggered power-project deliveries extending beyond.
Over 80% of revenue from repeat customers; end-market demand from cement, steel, power, mining and engineering described as steady, with no project holds despite the West Asia crisis.

Raw material volatility (tungsten, nickel, cobalt, molybdenum, chromium) is affecting margins; price variation clauses cover under 10% of the order book, with the rest fixed-price contracts. Management books raw materials on order and gives short offer validity on volatile items.
Price increases are ongoing, linked to input costs; management says customers are aware of raw material conditions.

Exports reach more than 35 countries including Southeast Asia, Middle East and Africa; Turkey operations are maturing, a new West Africa partner has been identified, and Singapore sales rose significantly in FY26.
Competitors named: Ador Fontech (merged into Ador Welding) and EWAC Alloys (now part of ESAB) in welding consumables and wear plates; ThyssenKrupp, ISGEC and Walchandnagar in heavy engineering.

qa_highlights.question: Why is standalone growth flat relative to consolidated, and will it normalise in FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said standalone plants were already at about 85% utilisation, capping execution in wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering; new capacity from Q1 FY27 should lift standalone growth to match consolidated.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin volatility (13% to 14.8%) driven by?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to raw material price lags on fixed-price contracts; gross margin may fall, but fixed and operating costs have been consolidated, so net margins improved with scale.

qa_highlights.question: How is the debtor-day gap versus Ador Fontech explained?
qa_highlights.answer: Debtors are at 98 days for FY26 due to large heavy-engineering shipments in March (about INR140 crores of Q4 sales, including roughly INR20 crores of rollers). Target is 80-85 days for FY27; welding consumables are cash-and-carry; heavy engineering is typically 60 days contractually but extends to 75-90 days in practice.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR650 crore revenue target be reached faster, with growth accelerating above 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects growth to rise as new facilities come online and expects INR650 crores in 2-3 years on run-rate basis; no additional capex is needed for that level, and INR100 crores of capex could support INR800-900 crores.

qa_highlights.question: When will railway and defence businesses contribute meaningful revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Railway developmental orders take 6-9 months to execute, with substantial revenue from next year after approved-vendor listing. Tejorup defence revenue is not expected in FY26 or significantly in FY27, pending prototype approval.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue contribution from new products such as steel mill rollers and VRM rollers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify, citing confidentiality; said steel mill roller revenue was significant last year, a first VRM order has been won, and shredder spare parts are under development.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility (tungsten, cobalt, nickel) on fixed-price contracts; gross margin pressure in FY27 with a lag in passing through costs.
Standalone profitability: Q4 standalone PAT fell 3.05% YoY despite revenue growth, and standalone growth depends on Unit 4 commissioning on schedule by end of Q1 2027.
Receivable days at 98 in FY26 with heavy-engineering payment cycles of 75-90 days; management's 80-85 target needs to be met.
Quarterly concentration: Q4 is seasonally large, and management expects Q4 to remain the biggest quarter.
Tejorup defence and railway developmental businesses carry lower initial margins and long gestation periods.
Management's stated 20%+ FY27 growth and 80-100 bps margin expansion are to be tracked against Q1 FY27 results.

544264|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 36.5% YoY to INR1,101.08 million, with order book up 20.4% QoQ to INR209 crores.
544264|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 36.5% YoY to INR1,101.08 million, with EBITDA excluding other income up 33.76% to INR141.54 million. The order book reached INR209 crores at 30 June 2026, with more than 80% stated as executable in FY27, and a ~INR100 crore capacity expansion is coming on stream in phases at Nagpur.

segments.commentary: Order book of INR26.42 crores. Management said growth in Q1 came across consumables, wear plates/parts and heavy engineering.

segments.name: Welding Consumables
segments.commentary: Order book of INR24.22 crores, described as a strong sequential increase driven by customers consolidating yearly requirements. Management said there was no one-off windfall.

segments.name: Defence

segments.name: Exports / International

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone margin fall from ~18% peak to ~13%, and is Q1 the bottom?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q1 FY26 standalone PAT included a one-time ~INR5 crore subsidiary dividend. Management expects margins to return to prior-year Q1 levels and rise 100-200 bps over the next 1-1.5 years.

544264|2026-09.headline: Diffusion Engineers Q4 FY25 revenue rose 38.55% YoY to INR1,024.48 million; FY25 revenue INR3,351.96 million, up 20.51%.
544264|2026-09.overview: Q4 FY25 was the company's first earnings call after its October 2024 listing. Revenue grew 38.55% YoY to INR1,024.48 million, with EBITDA (ex other income) up 82.55% to INR147.01 million and margin up 346 bps to 14.35%. FY25 revenue rose 20.51% to INR3,351.96 million, EBITDA ex other income rose 21.12% to INR470.76 million, and PAT rose 17% to INR360.40 million. Management is roughly doubling capacity with a INR100 crore capex programme, with the new capacity targeted by end FY26 and utilisation currently around 85%.

segments.name: Heavy engineering
segments.commentary: One of three product baskets, each stated to contribute roughly one-third of revenue. Management expects it, and wear parts, to grow faster than consumables; ~50-odd customers. Divisional EBITDA margins not disclosed.

segments.name: Wear plates and wear parts
segments.commentary: One of three equal-weight baskets; management says growth in FY25 was strong, alongside heavy engineering. Serves close to 1,000 customers. Replacement cycle is 18-24 months.

segments.name: Welding and anti-wear consumables
segments.commentary: One of three equal-weight baskets, said to carry higher margins than wear plates and heavy engineering, but grew more slowly in FY25. Flux core wire is ~7% of turnover and cold repair compounds ~3%.

segments.name: Services and rental
segments.commentary: Industrial services (on-site breakdown repair, kiln alignment) are ~1-2% of revenue. A new wear-part rental model has two ongoing contracts, already fully paid, with NBFC lease tie-ups planned.

guidance_outlook: Capacity to roughly double by end FY26 with INR100 crore capex: Nimji heavy engineering unit ~INR70 crore, B33 MIDC unit ~INR30 crore.
Target asset turnover of about 3x, in line with historical 3-3.25x; 80-85% utilisation expected within 2-3 years of commissioning.
Management aims to grow faster than the market and to improve margins; no forward revenue numbers given.
ROCE is about 15% at present, with an aspiration to match or beat pre-IPO levels.
Working capital to stay around 90-100 days given 6-9 month heavy equipment cycles and 90-100 day payment terms.
Planned 1.1 MW captive rooftop solar on the Nimji unit, funded from IPO objects.
capex_capacity: INR100 crore capex for FY26: Nimji heavy engineering unit ~INR70 crore and B33 MIDC unit ~INR30 crore.
Current utilisation about 85% on the existing capacity base; capacity to roughly double by end FY26.
Capex adds machining capability for larger and more precise parts, which management says few Indian suppliers offer.
Abu Dhabi service and manufacturing plant was due to go live in Q1 FY26 (this quarter).
Unit 4 has started flux-coated wire and wear plate production.
demand_pricing: Revenue growth attributed to timely execution of high-value orders and demand from cement, steel, power and engineering, with growth across all sectors.
Order book was cited as roughly INR100-120 crore; management says it keeps growing daily, and over 50% of orders come from repeat customers.
Around 23-25% of revenue goes through OEMs; the rest is direct to end clients, with a small channel-partner share.
Exports were 12-13% of FY25 revenue, down from 13-14% in FY24, though absolute exports are rising. Export margins are higher due to less competition.
About 80% of OE business is new projects and the rest is maintenance, which management describes as recurring.
Margin gains were attributed to volume-driven purchasing scale and low metal and raw-material prices in prior years.
Customers are moving to ready-to-fit and complete solutions rather than buying consumables themselves.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins be split across the three verticals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not disclose product-wise EBITDA margins. It said consumables and anti-wear carry higher margins than wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee and manufacturing costs rise sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said recruitment was started to gear up for the capex, and that gross margin should be read across raw material, stock purchases, inventory change and manufacturing expenses together.

qa_highlights.question: Is growth stagnant until new capacity comes online?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth will continue, with the new capacity making it more significant. It noted lead times differ by order mix.

qa_highlights.question: How much of heavy engineering is made in-house from own consumables and wear parts?
qa_highlights.answer: On average 20-30%, with a range of 15-50% depending on the order, excluding machining.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status and use of IPO capex funds?
qa_highlights.answer: The funds are held in fixed deposits with scheduled commercial banks and not in mutual funds. The mutual fund holdings come from free cash flow, mostly in equity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the other income of about INR5 crore in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: It is largely interest on IPO proceeds. Management said EBITDA excluding other income rose 21% to INR470 million in FY25.

risks_watch: Utilisation near 85% limits near-term volume growth until the INR100 crore capacity is commissioned by end FY26.
Working capital stays around 90-100 days; heavy equipment cycles of 6-9 months add inventory.
UK associate (21.5% stake, nickel and cobalt powders) booked losses from inventory revaluation; management says no similar losses are expected.
Metal price volatility, notably nickel, affects costs and margins.
Management did not disclose the revenue of the rental model or the economics of heavy engineering in detail; mentioned only two ongoing rental contracts.
Exports fell as a share of revenue to 12-13% in FY25 from 13-14% in FY24.
Margin expansion depends on exports and more complex parts; management declined to quantify.
544264|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on growth and capacity, with a clear capex plan, but evasive on segment margins, revenue split, forward numbers and the rental economics. Management deflected several questions as qualitative or said it would not share the figures.
key_quotes: So, we are approximately doubling our capacity. So, it will happen by end of this year, this financial year.
We have not used our I would say, IPO proceeds for any payments of all the vendors or debtors because the objects wanted reduction of working capital, which we did.
Generally, we do not give forward looking numbers, but definitely our aim is to grow more than the market.
So, the margin increase has happened because of the volume growth.

financial_highlights.change: +17% YoY from INR308.05 million; PAT margin 10.75%

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: INR100 crore capex (Nimji ~INR70 cr, B33 MIDC ~INR30 cr) is under construction to roughly double capacity by end FY26, with the Abu Dhabi plant due Q1 FY26 and Unit 4 already producing flux-coated wire and wear plates.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.why: Utilisation is about 85%, above the 80%+ threshold, and the INR100 crore programme is already committed, so a further capex announcement is likely as headroom is used up.

rows.why: Management gives no forward revenue numbers and only says it aims to grow faster than the market, so there is no guidance to raise.

rows.why: Plant was due to go live in Q1 FY26 and was in trial runs, adding a minor overseas capacity base.

rows.label: Order book of INR100-120 crore with repeat-customer base
rows.why: Order book of INR100-120 crore keeps growing daily and over 50% of orders come from repeat customers, supporting revenue visibility.

rows.label: Working capital held at 90-100 days
rows.why: Management guided working capital to stay around 90-100 days given 6-9 month heavy equipment cycles and 90-100 day payment terms, so no release is expected.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, the INR100 crore capacity doubling and the order book, but evasive on product-wise margins, revenue split, rental economics and forward numbers; analysts pushed on margin split, cost increases and the status of IPO funds.

544277|2026-03.headline: Waaree FY26 revenue rose ~84% to INR26,537 crore and operating EBITDA 117% to INR5,909 crore, but Q4 margin fell to ~18.6% on commodity, freight and mix pressures.
544277|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a record year: revenue from operations of INR26,537 crore (+84% YoY), operating EBITDA of INR5,909 crore (22.27% margin vs 18.84%) and PAT of INR3,884 crore (+101%). Q4 revenue was INR8,480 crore (+111% YoY) and operating EBITDA INR1,576 crore, with margin down sharply from the prior quarter as silver and copper costs, freight spikes, lower overseas mix and in-house DCR cell shortfall weighed. Management guided FY27 operating EBITDA to INR7,000-7,700 crore and framed the Waaree 2.0 capex (~$3.5 billion) as the driver, with most cell and module capex completing in FY27 and benefits from H2 FY27 onward. Operating cash conversion fell to about 27% as export shipments were stuck on logistics delays and inventory built up.

segments.name: Module manufacturing
segments.commentary: FY26 production 12.6 GW (+77%), sales about 12 GW; Q4 production 4.2 GW (+104% YoY) and Q4 sales 4.1 GW. Capacity ~26 GW, described as the largest non-Chinese module maker.

segments.name: Cell manufacturing
segments.commentary: Operational cell capacity 5.4 GW (largest in India); Q4 cell production 0.7 GW. A 10 GW cell facility is due in H2 FY27, taking cell capacity to ~15.4 GW.

segments.name: Revenue mix (FY26)
segments.commentary: Utility/IPP/C&I 34.7%, overseas 33%, retail 20.8%, EPC 11.6%. Retail revenue INR5,515 crore (+84%). Q4 overseas share fell to ~21% from ~32% in Q3.

segments.name: US manufacturing
segments.commentary: 1.6 GW plant ramped; 2.6 GW more to go live within six months, taking US capacity to 4.2 GW. IRA benefit ~$0.07/Wp, ~$40 million in FY26, to rise with new capacity.

segments.name: Order book
segments.commentary: ~INR53,000 crore excluding retail (~20% of revenue), up from ~INR47,000 crore a year ago but down ~INR7,000 crore QoQ per analyst. ~65-70% is overseas, to be delivered over 3-4 years. More than INR8,400 crore delivered already.

guidance_outlook: FY27 operating EBITDA guided at INR7,000-7,700 crore (about 20-25% growth on FY26 INR5,909 crore).
Management says the margin benefit from in-house DCR cells starts in H2 FY27 when the 10 GW cell line goes live; H1 is a transition.
Long-range planning assumption: 19-20% EBITDA margin sustained for a decade.
Cell utilisation assumed 80-85% for FY28 on 15.4 GW capacity; 28 GW modules, 4 GW inverters, 20,000 MVA transformers and 1 GW electrolyser to run at full throttle in FY28.
Capex of ~$3.5 billion (INR30,000 crore) over the next two years; core module and cell capex complete in FY27, ingot wafer and part of battery in FY28; full Waaree 2.0 benefits seen in FY29.
Cell line transition from M10R to G12R expected to lift output and realisation by 10-12% within about a quarter; module output back to ~330 MW a month within two months.
Investor Day to be held; enabling board resolution for fundraise of up to ~INR10,000 crore approved, with shareholder approval to follow.
capex_capacity: Battery (BESS): 20 GWh planned, phase 1 of 3.5 GWh in FY27 (Gujarat), phase 2 of 16.5 GWh in FY28; capex ~INR10,000 crore.
Ingot wafer: 10 GW at Nagpur, capex ~INR6,200 crore (up from INR5,100 crore earlier with 6 GW to 10 GW); completion FY28.
PV glass: 2,500 TPD approved at ~INR3,900 crore capex, production expected within 24 months; supports ~16-17 GW of modules.
Inverters: 4 GW at Sarodhi, Gujarat (~INR180 crore); 3 GW commissioned, remaining 1 GW in FY27.
Transformers: current ~4,000 MVA; adding 16,000 MVA to reach 20,000 MVA at Alwar (~INR192 crore) in FY27.
Hydrogen: 1 GW electrolyser at Dungri, Gujarat (~INR676 crore capex); electrolyser PLI INR444 crore and hydrogen PLI ~INR510 crore.
Acquired ~55% of Associated Power Structures Ltd (APSL) for ~INR1,225 crore for T&D entry; Oman polysilicon stake acquired for non-Chinese supply.
Module lines: 3 lines converted to G12R (ramping), 3 lines remain Mono PERC, 5 lines still on M10R TOPCon, to convert over about one quarter.
demand_pricing: Domestic DCR module pricing INR21-22/Wp; non-DCR utility INR15-16/Wp, with retail carrying a premium; commodity increases are being passed through to new orders.
Silver and copper cost increases, freight spikes and a lower overseas share weighed on Q4 margin; management said customers are now accepting the higher commodity-linked prices.
ALMM-II (domestic cell mandate) takes effect June 2026; C&I and mid-market decisions were deferred pending clarity, which slowed local offtake.
India installed 44.6 GW of solar in FY26; module consumption was about 50-55 GW. Management sees DCR-compliant cell capacity at ~30 GW for ALMM-II.
US FEOC rules from April 2026 require non-Chinese cells and components, which management says is driving new US orders.
BESS pricing around $110-120/MWh cited for India and US; BESS margin guided at 18-20% before policy support.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating EBITDA margin fall sharply QoQ, and what are the DCR and non-DCR realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited silver and copper cost spikes, freight cost surge, a lower overseas mix and DCR cell shortfall. DCR modules INR21-22/Wp; utility non-DCR INR15-16/Wp, with a retail premium.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the export mix low in Q4 and what is the order book composition?
qa_highlights.answer: Export shipments were stuck on Middle East logistics delays, so inventory rose. About 65-70% of the INR53,000 crore order book is overseas, delivered over 3-4 years; retail (~20% of revenue) is excluded.

qa_highlights.question: How will the FY27 EBITDA guidance of INR7,000-7,700 crore be achieved, and what drives margin?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 is a transition from 5.4 GW to 15.4 GW of cells; the 10 GW cell line in H2 lifts in-house DCR supply. Pre-startup costs for new projects are included in guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the ingot-wafer capex rise and its timeline move to FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity was raised from 6 GW to 10 GW and sites moved from Odisha to Gujarat and Nagpur, causing the delay. The new figure covers the full 10 GW.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cash conversion cycle and working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory built up because overseas shipments were delayed. Customer advances stayed steady but production nearly doubled, diluting working capital days. Management expects cash conversion of 70-100% at normalised inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What are the BESS unit economics and FY29 revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: BESS margin guided at 18-20% without policy support. Management declined to give FY29 revenue guidance, pointing to the 20 GWh capacity and $110-120/MWh pricing.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on the 10 GW cell line commissioning in H2 FY27 and on the G12R ramp; Q4 showed sharp margin compression.
Working capital and cash conversion (~27%) need to normalise as stuck export inventory ships.
ALMM-II timing uncertainty is deferring C&I and mid-market orders; order book fell ~INR7,000 crore QoQ.
Commodity (silver, copper) and freight volatility; pricing pass-through to new orders is unproven.
Execution risk on ~$3.5 billion capex across BESS, glass, ingot-wafer and US plants, plus fundraise of up to INR10,000 crore.
Overcapacity concerns in the module sector; management argues demand and supply balance once ALMM-II/III take effect.
544277|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and expansive on the long-term Waaree 2.0 story and on FY26 results. Noticeably defensive and detailed when explaining the Q4 margin drop, cash conversion and order-book sequential decline, often attributing them to temporary logistics and transition factors. Several answers on BESS economics, the fundraise, Indosolar and ALMM-II timing were deferred or left unquantified.

financial_highlights.change: Above prior guidance of INR5,500-6,000 crore
+70% YoY; margin fell sharply QoQ (analyst cited ~590 bps decline)
vs INR644 crore in Q4 FY25
Down from over 100% in prior period per analyst; management says 70-100% normalised

key_quotes: Our capital allocation follows a simple principle, book and build, which means every rupee we deploy is backed by confirmed demand and a clear path to returns.
The safest assumption there will be is your 19 %-20% margin consistent for a decade long at least.
So, we really don't foresee any scenario anytime next 5, 10 years of time will be the supply is going to be much higher than demand.
So, if you keep the inventory at normalized levels, the same number will go back to the normalized level of 70% to 100% conversion of cash from current 27%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY26 module production rose 77% to 12.6 GW and Q4 production hit 4.2 GW (+104% YoY), with cell utilisation assumed at 80-85% for FY28 on 15.4 GW, though Q4 cell output was only 0.7 GW and C&I orders are deferred by ALMM-II timing.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.when: already under way; ingot wafer FY28, BESS phase 2 FY28
rows.why: Waaree 2.0 capex of ~$3.5 billion (INR30,000 crore) over two years is committed, with the ingot wafer raised from INR5,100 crore to INR6,200 crore and a fundraise of up to INR10,000 crore enabled by the board, so the main announcements are already made.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY26 EBITDA of INR6,617 crore beat the INR5,500-6,000 crore guide, but FY27 guidance of INR7,000-7,700 crore is new and management flagged H1 FY27 as a transition with Q4 margin compression.

rows.why: BESS phase 1 of 3.5 GWh is planned in FY27 and the 10 GW cell line in H2 FY27 adds in-house DCR supply, with BESS margin guided at 18-20%.

rows.label: Cell line transition M10R to G12R lifts output and realisation 10-12%
rows.why: Three module lines are already converted to G12R and five lines still on M10R TOPCon are due to convert over about one quarter, with management citing a 10-12% lift in output and realisation.

rows.why: Operating cash conversion fell to about 27% as export shipments were held up by Middle East logistics delays, and management expects 70-100% at normalised inventory, but this is unquantified on timing.

544277|2026-06.headline: Waaree Q1 FY27 revenue rose 79.2% YoY to INR7,932 crore and order book hit a record INR61,500 crore, though operating EBITDA margin was 18.2%.
544277|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 79.2% YoY to about INR7,932 crore, with operating EBITDA up 44.4% to about INR1,440 crore at an 18.2% margin and PAT of INR892 crore (11% margin, up 15.4%). Management attributed margin pressure to higher global raw material costs, softer US exports from delayed clearances, and inventory built ahead of second-half-weighted dispatches. Order book rose to INR61,500 crore after INR16,000 crore of net inflows against about INR7,300 crore executed. Management reaffirmed FY27 operating EBITDA guidance of INR7,000-7,700 crore, pinning the margin recovery on rising captive cell integration and US local manufacturing.

segments.name: Revenue mix
segments.commentary: Utility IPP and C&I 39.7%, retail 30.2%, overseas 21.2%, EPC and O&M 8.9% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Utility/IPP/C&I share was 52.1% in FY25.

segments.name: Retail (B2C)
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR2,289 crore, up 130% YoY; management guides INR9,000-10,000 crore for FY27.

segments.name: Overseas / US
segments.commentary: US domestic revenue INR1,322 crore and direct exports INR287 crore. US plant produced about 230 MW in Q1, earning roughly USD12-13 million of IRA incentives.

segments.name: Cell manufacturing (India)
segments.commentary: 5.4 GW capacity at 62% utilisation; about 800 MW of DCR cell made in Q1. Integrated cell lines show 35-40% margin per management.

segments.name: Modules (India and US)
segments.commentary: India module capacity 24.2 GW at about 50% annualised utilisation; US module capacity 1.6 GW at about 59%. Management expects US utilisation of 75-80% in coming quarters.

segments.name: BESS / storage
segments.commentary: Automated BESS container capacity of 5.15 GWh started, versus 3.5 GWh originally planned. A 1,520 MWh BESS EPC order was won.

segments.name: Transmission and transformers
segments.commentary: Waaree Transpower began commercial production of a 17.6 MVA inverter-duty transformer. WRTL acquired about 55% of Associated Power Structures for about INR1,225 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 operating EBITDA guidance of INR7,000-7,700 crore reaffirmed.
FY28 ballpark of about INR7,000 crore EBITDA mentioned by Varun Goenka; FY28 expected to see about 16-18 GW module and about 10 GW cell production.
Cell-to-module integration ratio to rise from about 20% to about 65% within 2-3 quarters.
Cell production to rise from about 800 MW in Q1 to about 1.2 GW in Q2 and about 1.5 GW in Q3.
Module utilisation to reach 70-75% in Q3 and Q4; management expects 80-85% over 2-3 quarters as integration rises.
US IRA incentive receipts expected quarterly from Q3-Q4 FY27 via refund or sale of credits; US production of 400-500 MW per quarter from Q3.
Management aspires to a near INR1 lakh crore revenue vision in less than 4-5 years.
capex_capacity: Announced capex programme about INR31,500 crore; about INR9,450 crore deployed as of 30 June. Phasing is about 30% in FY27, 40% in FY28 and 30% in FY29.

FY27 additions: 2.6 GW US modules, 10 GW Indian cell (Gujarat, ALMM-II applied, equipment on site, commercial start expected from about Q3), 100 KTPA T&D EPC, 20 GVA transformers, 4 GW inverters, 1 GW electrolysers.
FY28: 10 GW ingot and wafer at Nagpur, construction started. FY29: 2,500 TPD solar glass (about INR3,900 crore, greenfield approved) and 16.5 GWh BESS plant.
Indian cell capacity to reach 15.4 GW against 24.2 GW module capacity by FY27-end; US BESS cell 3.5 GWh to commission within FY27, with 95% site construction done.
Potential QIP of about INR10,000 crore approved by Board and shareholders; timing depends on market conditions.
demand_pricing: Order book INR61,500 crore as of 28 July 2026 (25.2 GW), up from about INR53,000 crore at FY26-end; geographic mix India about 40%, US about 36%, exports about 24%.
Realisations per watt: exports USD0.25-0.26; DCR USD0.20-0.25; non-DCR USD0.13-0.14. Order book realisations seen at USD0.24-0.25 for near quarters; long-range DCR orders at USD0.21-0.22.
Non-DCR offtake delayed by developers in Q1; ALMM-II effective 1 June with about a 5-6 month window, leading to expected offtake from Q2.
Top 5 customers 27.1% of sales (from 33% in FY26); top 10 at 37.1% (from 47%).

544279|2026-09.headline: Godavari Biorefineries Q2 FY27 net loss narrowed to Rs15.2 crore as bio-based chemicals revenue rose 38.8% to Rs204.2 crore.
544279|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations rose 27.5% YoY to Rs549.2 crore and the company swung to a net profit of Rs10.9 crore versus a loss of Rs4.4 crore a year earlier. The bio-based chemicals segment was the main driver, with revenue up 38.8% to Rs204.2 crore and segment EBITDA up 47% to Rs22.1 crore. The integrated sugar, cogeneration and ethanol segment still posted a Rs19.3 crore EBITDA loss, though it improved from Rs23.1 crore a year earlier. Management said H2 is seasonally strong for sugar and ethanol and that the drought and feedstock-policy changes are pressuring that business.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q2 bio-based chemicals revenue beat (Rs204.2 crore vs Rs190 crore target) came from volume, debottlenecking or pricing, and what is needed to reach Rs240 crore per quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 revenue rose from about Rs140 crore a year ago to Rs204.2 crore on debottlenecking plus some volume and price gains tied to a supply disruption. The Rs240 crore run-rate is to come from the Rs25 crore debottlenecking investment, expected to start by April 2027, with market entry taking time.

qa_highlights.question: Who is the revenue mix moving between commodity products like ethyl acetate and specialty molecules, and what marks structural margin improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: About 52% of H1 FY27 chemicals revenue came from specialty products. Management said ethyl acetate may be pursued when market conditions justify it, but the structural strategy remains specialty bio-based chemicals.

qa_highlights.question: What utilisation levels are the cane and grain units running at, and can grain flexibility be increased?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the grain-based facility is running now and will depend on maize and rice economics and cane availability. Cane-based ethanol utilisation will fall on the government's diversion restriction, with sugar output rising instead.

qa_highlights.question: When will profitability reach shareholders in the medium term, and what are the DME and drug discovery timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 is seasonally loss-making and H2 profitable, and that chemicals are not seasonal. DME pilot results are due after March 2027. The breast cancer molecule trial needs CDSCO permission this quarter, with early efficacy data 6-9 months after trial start.

qa_highlights.question: What is the trial budget and the plan after preliminary efficacy results?
qa_highlights.answer: Preliminary efficacy trial budget is Rs15-20 crore. If results are positive, management plans to out-license the molecule to Indian or foreign pharma companies, since it is not a pharmaceutical company.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital allocation priority, and when would larger chemical capacity be added?
qa_highlights.answer: Capital allocation will shift to bio-based specialty chemicals, with only minor ethanol optimisation spend. Larger chemical capacity additions wait for larger customer off-take agreements.

qa_highlights.question: Why did bio-based chemicals margin rise only about 60 bps despite segment EBITDA up 47%, and why did inventory rise sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not address the margin gap directly; it reiterated the specialty strategy and Rs240 crore target. On inventory, it said the rise to about Rs260 crore is seasonal, with sugar stocks peaking in March and falling by September.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company managing feedstock procurement for the upcoming ethanol season, and what drives the sugar segment's profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is working with farmers on yield and regenerative agriculture, and is weighing cane, maize and FCI rice. It said H2 is always profitable and that H1 sugar realisations were slightly better than last year.

544280|2026-03.headline: Afcons posted its first-ever quarterly loss (Q4 net loss INR 89 crore) and FY26 PAT fell to INR 251 crore; no FY27 revenue or margin guidance given.
544280|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue fell 18% YoY to INR 2,777 crore and EBITDA dropped to INR 170 crore from INR 415 crore, with a net loss of INR 89 crore. Management blamed customer payment delays, overseas supply-chain disruption from the Middle East conflict, one-off provisions and marine cost overruns, and failure to cross margin-recognition thresholds on some projects. FY26 revenue was INR 12,322 crore (down 5.4%), EBITDA INR 1,439 crore (11.7% margin) and PAT INR 251 crore after a INR 76 crore Labour Code charge. Management guided FY26 order booking of INR 30,000 crore for FY27 but declined to give revenue or margin guidance until visibility improves.

segments.commentary: Management estimated about 25% of domestic projects were affected in March; UP Jal Jeevan Mission payments are being withheld until 100% completion, against a contractual stage-wise payment basis.

No revenue growth or EBITDA margin guidance for FY27 or Q1 FY27, citing geopolitical uncertainty, elongated award cycles and payment issues.
FY27 capex guided at about INR 725 crore; FY26 capex was INR 1,069 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 so far below the mid-quarter confidence expressed on the Q3 call, and what drove the miss?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q4 customer payments did not come as in the past 15-20 years; Afcons chose liquidity over growth, funding projects only up to limits, and overseas supply disruption in March (fuel, gas, logistics) hit execution.

qa_highlights.question: What are the one-off items in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Total one-offs of about INR 260-265 crore: about INR 160 crore of Q4 provisions (including an ECL matrix shift), a significant arbitration-related provision, and extra cost on a marine project. Management said no further provisions were made in Q1 FY27 to date.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of finance cost and the rise in interest?
qa_highlights.answer: About 40% of customer advances in FY26 were interest-bearing versus a partial-year effect in FY25; average borrowing rose and rate cuts did not fully offset the increase.

qa_highlights.answer: Payment delays are widespread; apart from UP Jal Jeevan Mission and a Gabon project, no specific names were disclosed. Projects below 10% completion carry about two months of receivables.

qa_highlights.question: Why no guidance when order book is about INR 60,000 crore after inflows?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited long gestation projects (four dams of about five years; HSR package extended 12-15 months), elongated award cycles, and fuel and geopolitical uncertainty, saying revenue visibility is not yet adequate.

qa_highlights.answer: Gabon bank guarantee invoked and paid; the contract was already loss-provided with no margin recognised, and about 92% complete.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 attrition higher, and will other expenses moderate?
qa_highlights.answer: Attrition rose because seasonal headcount exited after open enrolment. Other expenses rose on IT and AI investment plus some asset write-offs from centre rationalisation; management expects them to stay high.

544282|2026-06.headline: Sagility Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27.6% YoY to INR 19,635m; FY27 margin guidance held at 24-25% despite a 120 bps minimum-wage hit.
544282|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 27.6% YoY (15.2% in constant currency) to INR 19,635 million, with organic growth of 27.3% in INR and 14.9% in constant currency, helped by the CareSeed acquisition closed 11 June 2026. Sequentially, reported revenue fell because about $24.8 million of Q4 open-enrolment revenue did not recur, but steady-state organic revenue grew 5.1% QoQ in constant currency. Adjusted EBITDA rose 27.9% to INR 4,716 million at a 24.0% margin (down from 24.9% in Q4), and adjusted PAT rose 35.1% to INR 2,697 million at 13.7%. Management reiterated low double-digit FY27 organic constant-currency growth and the 24-25% margin range, with the wage impact absorbed via efficiencies and FX.

qa_highlights.question: What share of minimum-wage staff is in Karnataka and Telangana, and is the 120 bps impact recurring and recoverable?
qa_highlights.answer: Less than 15-20% of employees are outside Karnataka and Telangana; the 120 bps impact includes cascading pay-parity effects; full mitigation expected in 12-18 months via efficiencies and expansion in other states.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the low double-digit guidance not higher given 5% QoQ underlying growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said QoQ growth should not be extrapolated; 14.9% organic growth in Q1 and confidence in double-digit growth for FY27 were reiterated, with narrower guidance at end-Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a pricing lever in the 15% growth, and what is the split between new and old clients?
qa_highlights.answer: No pricing increases were taken; the client-level split of growth was not available and will be provided later.

qa_highlights.question: Why was margin guidance not raised despite 24% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-quarter minimum wage impact starts Q2 (about double the Q1 impact); FX gains and efficiencies offset; lower end is expected to be exceeded if the wage impact is lower.

qa_highlights.question: How much seasonal revenue was in FY25 vs FY26 and what drives FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Seasonal revenue was about $20 million in Q3+Q4 FY25 (about 3%) and about $50 million in FY26 (about 6%), boosted by BroadPath and a clinical seasonal client; FY27 expected at a similar percentage.

qa_highlights.question: Is M&A pipeline focused where?
qa_highlights.answer: Clinical, provider-side and healthcare technology capabilities; direct client-acquisition M&A is difficult given existing vendor relationships.

544282|2026-09.headline: Sagility Q2 FY27 revenue rose 22.5% YoY in INR to INR 20,321 mn, adjusted EBITDA margin hit 26.3%, and FY27 margin guidance was raised to 25-26%.
544282|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR 20,321 mn ($212.6 mn), up 22.5% YoY in INR and 12.2% in constant currency, with organic growth of 11.9% in constant currency. Adjusted EBITDA rose 23% to INR 5,353 mn at a 26.3% margin, the highest in six quarters, helped by operating efficiencies, FX tailwinds and geo mix despite higher statutory wage costs. Management acquired Chirok Health LLC (closed October 21, 2026) to build a mid-cycle RCM capability and push provider growth, and raised FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 25-26% from 24-25%. The company now holds a net cash position of INR 1,127 mn, and management expects open enrolment/AEP revenue to be slightly lower than last year.

segments.commentary: Accounted for 10.1% of Q2 revenue and has grown at about 10-11%, lagging payers. Revenue tapered from some discrete projects with one provider client; Chirok acquisition is intended to accelerate this segment.

TTM revenue to Sep 2026 of $13 mn, adjusted EBITDA margin 35.8%, net revenue retention above 115%, 750+ employees mostly in India. Consideration $20 mn upfront plus up to $12.35 mn earn-out tied to CY27-CY28 revenue targets.

segments.commentary: Integrated into clinical practice; strengthens Medicare Advantage quality capability and adds mid- and small-sized clients. Contributed to the gap between reported 22.5% and organic 22.2% growth.

guidance_outlook: FY27 organic revenue growth guidance of low double digits in constant currency maintained; Chirok and CareSeed revenue sits on top of organic guidance.
FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance raised to 25-26% from 24-25%; management said it sees 24-26% as the structural range, with possible marginal upside if AI productivity gains are retained.

OE/AEP revenue expected to be slightly lower than last year, roughly 100 bps lower as a share of total revenue (last year about 6%); marginally below flat YoY per CFO; subject to change over coming weeks.

Staffing to capacity for AEP season with some flex capacity available.
105 active client groups; all top 10 client groups above $20 mn TTM revenue for the first time.
demand_pricing: Deal ACV up 18.2% YoY to $40.2 mn in Q2, from wins across 31 existing clients and one new client.

Clients making more deliberate, senior-level buying decisions for large transformation deals; pipeline skewed to managed services and mid-market Blues plans.
Agentic AI deployments: Synchrony Claims Lifecycle (claims adjudication) and Synchrony RCM Lifecycle (denials and appeals), with humans in the loop.
Management said provider deals have historically been smaller; gross margin difference between payer and provider is about 200-300 bps and deal-specific.
On AI pricing, most productivity gains will be passed to clients, with some retained.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin improvement and what supports the raised guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO cited operating efficiencies, a small FX tailwind from Q1 to Q2, and favourable geo mix; he expects FX to stay broadly at current levels and efficiencies to continue for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: How much could open enrolment contribution fall this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh said about 100 bps lower than last year's roughly 6% of revenue on current visibility; CFO said it is marginally below flat YoY at this early stage.

qa_highlights.question: Is Chirok a step-up in provider mix, and is there an explicit provider target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the goal is a much larger provider share over time but gave no explicit 2-3 year target; provider share is about 10% today. Investment is mainly the Chirok deal plus a dedicated provider go-to-market team, with no major margin impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why is provider growth lagging, and what is Chirok's growth history?
qa_highlights.answer: Provider growth has been 10-11% with some revenue taper from discrete projects at one client. Chirok revenue dipped in 2023-24 when one client's volumes fell, then recovered; management said the 35.8% margin is broadly on the same basis as Sagility's adjusted EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Is there conflict in serving both payers and providers?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh said there is no inherent conflict, citing about 15 years of running both businesses and claims-denial friction the company helps resolve.

qa_highlights.question: Will margin stay in 24-26% range or structurally rise with AI?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh said the range remains 24-26%, with possible gradual upside if the company keeps some AI productivity benefits; most gains are expected to flow to clients.

qa_highlights.question: What are the minimum wage impacts and delivery centre trends?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the full minimum wage impact is baked into guidance (Q2 about INR 148 mn vs INR 70 mn in Q1), with Karnataka and Telangana effective end May and 1 June. The drop in site count reflects campus consolidation.

risks_watch: OE/AEP revenue is running slightly below last year, and the number could still shift over the coming weeks.
Chirok revenue per headcount is well below a listed Indian provider peer; management could not explain the gap and will follow up. Chirok pricing is said to be at market.
Chirok's AI disruption exposure in mid-cycle RCM: management says outpatient coding is most vulnerable, while inpatient coding is less exposed.
Provider growth has lagged payers; watch whether Chirok and cross-selling lift provider growth above 10-11%.
Statutory minimum wage increases in Karnataka and Telangana are a continuing cost headwind; any stay would be upside.
Q2 margin benefited from FX and geo mix, so sustainability depends on FX staying near current levels.
Earn-out payments on Chirok (up to $12.35 mn) and the $10 mn+ payment integrity deal depend on revenue milestones, so timing is uncertain.
Possible acquisitions: management said it stays open to clinical capability or client-focused tuck-ins, but named no specific target.

544283|2026-03.headline: ACME Solar Q4 FY26 revenue rose 31% YoY to INR705 crore, FY26 revenue INR2,507 crore (+59%), with 2.3 GW of merchant BESS now running.
544283|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total revenue was INR705 crore (+31% YoY), including INR157 crore of other income, and FY26 revenue was INR2,507 crore (+59%) on capacity addition and higher CUF. PAT was INR138 crore for the quarter (19.6% margin) and INR498 crore for FY26 (19.9%), with management citing EBITDA margins above 90%. Management said about 2.3 GW of BESS is now commissioned and earning on merchant and short-term contracts at roughly INR2.2 crore per day. Management also flagged a timeline shift: most of the 1.5 GW generation commissioning and the 10 GWh BESS target depend on CTU substations, some of which are delayed by up to about 6 months.

segments.commentary: About 2.3 GWh of BESS is commissioned, mostly in March, and earns about INR2.2 crore per day net (over INR60 crore per month) from tariff arbitrage. Round-trip efficiency is 88-90%. Management said the Q3 battery contribution was negligible.

Battery target of about 10 GWh for the next calendar year: roughly 8.5 GWh merchant and 1.5 GWh in FDRE format. Management said the 10 GWh target is achievable on connectivity and financing; supply and geopolitics are the main uncertainties.
Around 2.5 GW of connectivity at operational substations (Fatehgarh-1, Fatehgarh-2 under STOA, Bikaner-3) is ready for BESS discharge at night.
Under-construction portfolio of 5.1 GW (total pipeline 8,071 MW) with PPA-signed capacity of 3,280 MW; PPA-signed projects expected to be commissioned by FY28.
Management expects a run-rate EBITDA jump as battery revenue starts; a 75-80% EBITDA margin is expected on merchant BESS at INR6 tariff arbitrage.

Gross block rose about INR3,460 crore in FY26, of which about INR1,000-1,100 crore is battery.

Capital advances of about INR323 crore, mainly battery (10% advance against bank guarantee) and turbines (20% advance). Management said solar module capex is being deferred until the LTA is operational.
Under-construction portfolio added 301 MW of peak-power FDRE with SECI in the quarter; total under construction is 5.1 GW, requiring about 17 GWh of BESS.

Commissioning timeline: NTPC hybrid solar ready, LTA by December 2026; Pachora wind component a couple of quarters later; SJVN Fatehgarh full FDRE by FY27 end (LTA March 2027). Pavagada and Anantapur are targeted this year per CTU timelines.
demand_pricing: India peak demand hit 256 GW on 25 April 2026, against 250 GW in May 2024. Electricity consumption grew 8.9% in April 2026.

India added about 55 GW of RE in FY26 (cumulative 283 GW). Management expects peak-power and FDRE/BESS-linked bids to dominate, with 15-20 GW of bids this year (fewer than last year) and state plus central tenders of 20-30 GW.

qa_highlights.question: What battery capex was incurred and how much BESS capacity was commissioned?

qa_highlights.question: What is the run-rate EBITDA from existing capacity?

qa_highlights.question: Is there curtailment, and how is future project allocation shaped?

qa_highlights.question: Why is gross block growing faster than run-rate EBITDA?

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk from LOA conversion and CERC connectivity rules?

544283|2026-06.headline: ACME Solar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 63% YoY to INR954 crore and EBITDA 56% to INR831 crore, with BESS contributing INR226 crore.

BESS commissioning reached about 3.62 GWh cumulative, and the BESS commissioning guidance was pulled forward to more than 10 GWh by FY27 from calendar 2027. qa_highlights.answer: Management said substation timelines of 2028 to early 2029 carry buffer for 6-12 months of delay. It has 8.5 GW of PPAs and expects 3-4 GW more soon, targeting 12 GW contracted by 2029 and 15 GW by 2030, with the tie-ups achievable by end of calendar 2027.

544285|2026-06.headline: Swiggy guides Quick Commerce contribution margin to 0 to -100 bps for growth, with 4-week cumulative NOV growth at 10% vs 1% prior.
544285|2026-06.overview: Swiggy's Q1 FY27 call (held July 30, 2026) centred on a deliberate pivot from contribution-margin protection to growth in Quick Commerce (Instamart). Management said it reached contribution margin breakeven, closing the last quarter at -0.2%, and now guides to a 0 to -100 bps range to fund store expansion, speed, serviceability and assortment. Take-rate gains were attributed to brand monetisation, advertising and user-fee changes, with management calling them sustainable. Food delivery growth was about 18% adjusted for cancellations, with 18-20% YoY guidance maintained, and management dismissed zero-commission competition from Toing's rivals as unsustainable. Toing, the new value-led food platform, is loss-making and was a major focus, with a Capital Markets Day planned for the following week.

segments.commentary: Contribution margin reached breakeven, last closed at -0.2%, with guidance of 0 to -100 bps. Plans to add more stores this quarter than in the last four quarters, all in existing cities; network utilisation about 40%.

segments.name: Food Delivery
segments.commentary: Adjusted growth about 18% YoY; YoY guidance 18-20% maintained. Take rate about 3%, with a target of 5%; management expects steady margin accretion.

segments.name: Platform Innovation (Toing, Snacc closed)
segments.commentary: Losses increased, mainly from Toing marketing to acquire users; Snacc closure last quarter left some residual operating costs. Roughly one-third of Toing users are existing Swiggy users. Toing is excluded from B2C GOV reporting.

guidance_outlook: Quick Commerce contribution margin guided to a range of 0 to -100 bps, assuming no change in competitive intensity; management says it would moderate if competition changes sharply.

Food delivery YoY growth guidance of 18-20% maintained.

Overall cash breakeven expected within about two quarters, supported by food delivery margin expansion and treasury income; platform innovation funding excluded until PMF and BMF are achieved.
Capital Markets Day / Investor Day scheduled the following week to cover Toing in more detail.

Some hyper-local stores are capacity-constrained at 2,500-3,000 orders per day, driving the new store additions.
Network-level store utilisation is about 40%.
Fixed costs from new stores, including 30-60-90 day ramp costs, are expensed within contribution margin and not capitalised, per management.
demand_pricing: Management says growth will come mainly from transacting user base and frequency rather than AOV, which it is not banking on going forward.
Monetisation (brand take rate, advertising, user fees) drove a large part of the 4-5 quarter improvement to CM breakeven; management says these revenues are sustainable.
Advertising is described as meaningfully kicking in, with inventory and product features being added to the app.
Competition: market has 7-8 players; management sees competitors operating at double-digit negative CM, and expects any new food entrants to target affordability rather than premium.
Toing uses lower commissions than Swiggy so restaurants can offer everyday low prices; management says commission will not be zero in practice.

Instamart delivery-fee line in fully loaded revenue appeared to be zero this quarter versus about INR3 per order previously (analyst observation); management did not confirm and referred to the adjusted revenue walk on page 16.

qa_highlights.question: How should we think about QC strategy: growth at expense of margin or vice versa, and what is the take-rate sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management prioritises growth within a 0 to -100 bps CM band. Take-rate gains come from brand negotiations, advertising and user-fee monetisation, which management says will not reverse.

qa_highlights.question: Is the food delivery zero-commission model a threat?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohit Kapoor argued zero commission is not sustainable; costs must be recovered from restaurants, consumers or delivery partners. Competition is expected in affordability, not premium.

qa_highlights.question: Wage hike and last-mile cost escalation?
qa_highlights.answer: Annual salary revision sits below CM. Minimum wage hikes in some states affect picking and packing; impact described as not material. Last-mile cost rose on seasonal factors including elections and harvest migration; efficiency offset kept the YoY dip to 20 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Are competitors capitalising costs or securitising payables?
qa_highlights.answer: Rahul Bothra said Swiggy does not capitalise employee, tech token or store costs, and is not aware of payables securitisation practices by peers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Instamart growth plan and store expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth from transacting users and frequency; more stores in existing cities as hyper-local stores hit 2,500-3,000 orders/day. Spend priorities are store expansion, speed and serviceability, and selection availability.

qa_highlights.question: Why did platform frequency decline and is private-label conflict with ads a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it culled low-value MTUs over recent quarters, and QC's lower frequency dilutes the blended metric. Private brands carry higher margins and are experience-driven, so conflict with ads was not seen as material.

544285|2026-09.headline: Swiggy Q2 FY27: Quick commerce NOV grew 13.4% QoQ with 1.3 million MTUs added, while Toing investment stays range-bound and food margin target of 5% of GOV is reaffirmed.
544285|2026-09.overview: Management reported a return to growth in quick commerce, with NOV up 13.4% QoQ, 1.3 million MTUs added, and orders per dark store per day up about 9% sequentially to close to 1,200. Food delivery guidance of 18-20% YoY growth on the standalone business was reiterated, with Adjusted EBITDA up about INR 50 crore for the quarter and take rate above 26%. Toing, the affordability platform, is being run as a range-bound investment; management asked for another quarter or two before judging whether it is a scalable model. Quick commerce contribution margin guidance is 0 to -100 bps, with 100 bps Adjusted EBITDA improvement guided for Q3, and a move to an inventory model starting mid-quarter.

segments.commentary: Four quarters old and run as range-bound investment. About 2 in 3 users are new to the platform, dual-app users show 25% higher orders per user, and retention is better than the core app. 70-80% of users are under 30 years old.

Present in 130+ cities with no near-term plan to expand geographic coverage; growth will come from densification within existing cities.

Quick commerce pricing intervention was cited by an analyst as lowering NOV-to-GOV ratio in the current quarter; management attributed growth to cohorts, retention and differentiated assortment.

Monetisation (commission, ads, consumer fees) has been flat for three quarters per an analyst; management says it is working with brands on co-created assortment and will evolve consumer fees over time.
Gross margin fell about 110-120 bps QoQ in quick commerce, per an analyst, linked to private label mix; management said 60 bps added in the previous quarter was partly reinvested.

qa_highlights.question: How should losses in quick commerce evolve and will Swiggy refocus on Tier-2 markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quick commerce returned to growth with 13.4% QoQ NOV growth and 1.3 million MTUs added, and that it is not looking to expand geographically beyond its current footprint of around 130 cities.

qa_highlights.question: Is Toing an experiment or ready to scale, and what metrics decide this?
qa_highlights.answer: Management asked for another one to two quarters before deciding. Metrics are repeat-user unit economics in early cities, customer acquisition cost as the base expands, and delivery cost reduction; investment is discretionary and range-bound.

qa_highlights.question: Is the contribution margin trajectory in quick commerce improving?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 0 to -100 bps contribution margin with sequential improvement and 100 bps Adjusted EBITDA improvement in Q3, with the inventory model contributing no benefit in the current quarter.
